questions.stem: A 2019 divorce decree provides that Alex pay alimony of $10,000 per year to Blair, to be reduced by 20% on their child's 18th birthday. During the tax year, Alex paid $7,000 directly to Blair and $3,000 for Blair's tuition to an accredited university. What amount, if any, of these payments should be reported as income in Blair's income tax return for the year?
questions.explanation:
After 2018, alimony is no longer included in taxable income, nor is it deductible.

Since the divorce decree was issued in 2019, the alimony is not reported as income in Blair's 2019 income tax return (nor is it a deduction for Alex).

("$7,000") Under pre-2018 rules, amounts paid on behalf of Blair (eg, to a university) are considered to be taxable alimony.

("$8,000" / "$10,000") Under pre-2018 rules, Blair reports $8,000 as income from alimony because the $10,000 annual payment decreases by 20% when the child reaches 18 years of age. IRS rules reclassify this $2,000 portion as disguised child support instead of alimony.
questions.explanationJa: 2018年より後に成立した離婚判決に基づく扶養料（alimony）は、受取人の課税所得に含まれず、支払人も控除できない。本問の判決は2019年なので、Blairが所得として報告する金額は$0である。大学の学費として第三者に支払った$3,000を扶養料に含めて$7,000以外も課税とする考え方や、子の18歳到達時の20%減額部分$2,000を偽装された養育費とみなして$8,000を所得とする考え方は、いずれも2018年以前の旧ルールの扱いである。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Individual Taxation Q.1

questions.stem: A taxpayer discovered an error that had been made in a previously filed tax return. The taxpayer should

choices.label: A
choices.text: File an amended return on Form 1040-X as long as the error is detected within 3 years of when the return was originally filed.

choices.label: B
choices.text: File an amended return on Form 1040-X as long as the error is detected within 5 years of when the return was originally filed.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Adjust the amounts in the current year's Form 1040 as long as the error is detected within 3 years of when the return was originally filed.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Adjust the amounts in the current year's Form 1040 as long as the error is detected within 5 years of when the return was originally filed.

questions.explanation:
Individual taxpayers report their annual tax activities to the IRS on Form 1040. Although taxpayers and tax practitioners try to file accurate returns, a tax return may contain an error. If an error is discovered and the statute of limitations period has not expired, an amended tax return should be filed to correct the error using Form 1040-X.

The statute of limitations is a law that establishes the period of time in which a taxpayer can amend a tax return or the IRS can assess a tax deficiency. It generally is 3 years. Therefore, Form 1040-X must be filed within 3 years of the date the incorrect return originally was filed ("File an amended return on Form 1040-X as long as the error is detecte…").

("Adjust the amounts in the current year's Form 1040 as long as the err…" / "Adjust the amounts in the current year's Form 1040 as long as the err…") When an error is detected on a previously filed tax return, the taxpayer must use Form 1040-X. The error may not be corrected by adjusting the current Form 1040.
questions.explanationJa: 過去に提出した申告書に誤りを見つけた場合、時効期間内であればForm 1040-Xで修正申告を行う。修正申告やIRSによる追徴課税が可能な時効期間は原則3年なので、Form 1040-Xは当初申告から3年以内に提出しなければならない。過去の誤りを当年のForm 1040の金額で調整して直すことは認められない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Individual Taxation Q.2

questions.stem:
Which of the following is (are) among the requirements to enable a taxpayer to be classified as a qualifying widow(er)?
I. A dependent has lived with the taxpayer for six months
II. The taxpayer has maintained the cost of the principal residence for six months
I | II

choices.label: A
choices.text: Yes | Yes

choices.label: B
choices.text: Yes | No

choices.label: C
choices.text: No | Yes

choices.label: D
choices.text: No | No

questions.explanation:
The qualifying widow(er) status is available for the two subsequent tax years after the spouse's death. To qualify, a taxpayer generally must:

Have been eligible to file jointly with the deceased spouse for the tax year of death.

Be unmarried (cannot remarry).

Have a dependent child who lived with the taxpayer for the entire tax year ("Yes | Yes" / "Yes | No").

Have paid more than half of the home's upkeep for the tax year ("Yes | Yes" / "No | Yes").
questions.explanationJa: 適格寡婦（夫）の地位は配偶者死亡年の翌2年間に認められ、死亡年に共同申告が可能だったこと、再婚していないこと、扶養する子がその課税年度の全期間にわたり同居していること、家屋の維持費の半分超を負担していることが要件である。扶養家族の同居は「6か月」ではなく通年が求められ、住居費用も「6か月間の負担」ではなく年間維持費の半分超の負担が求められる。したがって、問われている2つの条件はいずれも要件ではない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Individual Taxation Q.3

questions.stem: Evan, an individual, has a 40% interest in EF, an S corporation. At the beginning of the year, Evan's basis in EF was $2,000. During the year, EF distributed $100,000 and reported operating income of $200,000. What amount should Evan include in gross income?
questions.explanation: Income with respect to an S corporation is passed through to the shareholders without regard to distributions and would be reported on the shareholder's individual tax return. In this case, Evan owns a 40% interest in EF, so he would report $80,000 of the $200,000 income reported by EF as part of his gross income.
questions.explanationJa: S corporationの所得は、分配の有無にかかわらず持分に応じて株主に配分（パススルー）され、株主の個人申告書で報告される。Evanの持分は40%なので、EFの営業利益$200,000のうち$80,000（$200,000×40%）を総所得に含める。$100,000の分配額は所得の計算には関係しない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Individual Taxation Q.4

questions.stem: Chrisp, a freelance photographer, uses the cash method for business. The tax year ends on December 31. Which of the following should not be included in the determination of Chrisp's gross income for the current year?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Chrisp owns controlling shares of a closely held corporation and is planning to delay the bonus payment from the corporation until January of the next year. Bonus was authorized on December 15 of the current year and may be drawn at any time.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Chrisp received a check from a client on December 28 of the current year for a family portrait produced on December 22 of the current year. The check was dated December 23 of the current year but was not deposited until January 4 of the following year.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A client notified Chrisp on December 27 of the current year that a check was ready. The check was not picked up until January 4 of the following year.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Chrisp received a dividend check on January 4 of the following year. The dividends were declared payable on December 30 of the current year.

questions.explanation:
For income tax purposes, cash-basis taxpayers must report income in the period in which it is actually or constructively received, regardless of when it was earned. An item is constructively received when it is:

In the taxpayer's possession and control, or

Available without substantial restrictions or limits on the taxpayer's ability to use the funds.

A taxpayer may not defer possession or access to the income to avoid receipt. For example, postponing the pickup of a check for services performed until next year will not prevent constructive receipt ("A client notified Chrisp on December 27 of the current year that a ch…"). However, the declaration of a dividend does not constitute constructive receipt because the taxpayer does not have access to the funds until the check is received.

("Chrisp owns controlling shares of a closely held corporation and is p…") As the bonus was authorized and the funds were available to be drawn on December 15, Chrisp constructively received the bonus in December.

("Chrisp received a check from a client on December 28 of the current y…") The requirements for constructive receipt are met when a check is received on December 28, not when the check is deposited.
questions.explanationJa: 現金主義の納税者は、稼得時期にかかわらず、所得を現実に受領したか擬制的に受領した期に計上する。資金が手元にあるか、実質的な制約なく利用可能であれば擬制受領となり、小切手の受取りを翌年に延ばしても受領を先送りできない。12月に支給が承認されいつでも引き出せた賞与、12月28日に受け取った小切手（入金日は無関係）、12月27日に準備ができていた小切手はいずれも当年の所得である。一方、配当は宣言されただけでは資金を利用できないため擬制受領にならず、小切手を受け取った翌年1月4日の所得となる。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Individual Taxation Q.5

questions.stem:
A taxpayer began living in a nursing home this year in order to receive medical care for a specific condition. The taxpayer has AGI of $25,000 and incurred the following unreimbursed expenses:

Nursing home health care costs | $5,000
Nursing home meal and lodging costs | 8,000
Prescription drugs | 1,500

What amount may the taxpayer deduct from AGI this year as an itemized deduction?
questions.explanation:
Unreimbursed medical expenses are allowed as an itemized deduction to the extent the amount exceeds 7.5% of AGI. Allowable expenses include most medical services, equipment, and prescription drugs.

When a taxpayer resides in a nursing home or similar institution, the deductibility of the costs depends on the reason the individual is at the facility. If the reason is primarily for obtaining medical care, the entire cost, including meals and lodging, is deductible as a medical expense. However, if the primary reason is other than medical, only the costs for medical expenses and nursing care are deductible as a medical expense.

Since the taxpayer's primary reason for being in the nursing home is to receive medical care, the medical deduction is $12,625.

If an individual resides in a nursing home primarily to obtain medical care, the entire cost (including meals and lodging) is deductible as a medical expense.
questions.explanationJa: 未補填の医療費はAGIの7.5%を超える部分が項目別控除となる。ナーシングホームに入所した主な理由が医療を受けることであれば、食事・宿泊費を含む全費用が医療費になる（医療以外が主目的なら医療・看護部分のみ）。本問は医療目的の入所なので、医療費合計は$14,500（$5,000＋$8,000＋$1,500）、そこから$1,875（$25,000×7.5%）を差し引いた$12,625が控除額である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Individual Taxation Q.6

questions.stem: A single taxpayer has adjusted gross income of $40,000 in the current year. During the year, a hurricane causes $4,100 damage to the taxpayer's personal use car, on which the taxpayer has no damage insurance. The area in which the damage occurred was a federally declared disaster area. The taxpayer purchased the car for $20,000. Immediately before the hurricane, the car's fair market value was $11,000, and immediately after the hurricane its fair market value was $6,900. Assuming the taxpayer elects to itemize deductions, what amount should the taxpayer deduct as a casualty loss for the current year after all threshold limitations are applied?
questions.explanation:
The deduction for personal casualty losses is now generally limited to losses attributable to federally declared disasters through 2025. Accidental breakage and progressive deterioration (termites) are not casualty events.

The casualty loss is measured by the decrease in the asset's fair market value (FMV) caused by the event but is limited to the asset's adjusted tax basis. Once the loss is calculated, it must be reduced by all of the following limitations:

Insurance and government reimbursements

$100 per event

10% of adjusted gross income (AGI)

In this scenario, the taxpayer's casualty loss is deductible because it happened as a result of a federally declared disaster. Therefore, the taxpayer's casualty loss deduction for the current year is calculated as follows:

FMV of car before disaster: $11,000
Less: FMV after disaster: (6,900)
Total loss (lower than its $20,000 adjusted tax basis): $4,100
Less limitations:
Insurance reimbursement |  | (0)
De minimis $100 per event |  | (100)
10% of AGI ($40,000 × 10%) |  | (4,000)
Casualty loss deduction |  | $0

.line{
border-bottom:1px solid #000000;
}
questions.explanationJa: 個人の災害損失の控除は、原則として連邦政府指定の災害地域で生じた損失に限られる。損失額は災害による公正市場価値の下落額（調整後取得原価が上限）で測り、そこから保険等の補填額、1件当たり$100、AGIの10%を差し引く。本問の損失は$4,100（$11,000－$6,900、取得原価$20,000より小さい）で、保険補填$0、$100、AGIの10%である$4,000（$40,000×10%）を控除すると残りはなく、控除額は$0となる。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Individual Taxation Q.7

questions.stem: Nare, an accrual-basis taxpayer, owns a building which was rented to Mott under a ten-year lease expiring August 31, 20X8. On January 2, 20X2, Mott paid $30,000 as consideration for cancelling the lease. On November 1, 20X2, Nare leased the building to Pine under a five-year lease. Pine paid Nare $10,000 rent for the two months of November and December, and an additional $5,000 for the last month's rent. What amount of rental income should Nare report in its 20X2 income tax return?
questions.explanation: The $30,000 received for termination of the lease is reported as rental income. Also, even though Nare is an accrual basis taxpayer, rent collected in advance must be reported when received, so that both the $10,000 collected for November and December of the current year and the $5,000 collected in advance for the last month's rent is included in the current year income tax return.
questions.explanationJa: 賃貸借契約の解約対価として受け取った$30,000は賃貸収入として課税される。また、発生主義の納税者であっても前受家賃は受領時に課税されるため、11月・12月分の$10,000に加え、最終月分として前払いされた$5,000も当年の所得に含める。したがって当年の賃貸収入は$45,000（$30,000＋$10,000＋$5,000）である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Individual Taxation Q.8

questions.stem:
Randolph is a single individual who always claims the standard deduction. Randolph received the following in the current year:

Wages | $22,000
Unemployment compensation | $6,000
Pension distribution (100% taxable) | $4,000
A state tax refund from the previous year | $425

What is Randolph's gross income?
questions.explanation: Each listed item of income would be included in gross income except the state tax refund. The state tax refund would only be included if Randolph itemized deductions in the prior tax year and claimed a deduction for the state taxes.
questions.explanationJa: 賃金、失業給付、全額課税の年金分配はいずれも総所得に含まれる。州税還付金は、前年に項目別控除を選択して州税を控除していた場合にのみ課税されるが、Randolphは常に標準控除を使っているので含めない。したがって総所得は$32,000（$22,000＋$6,000＋$4,000）である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Individual Taxation Q.9

questions.stem: An individual taxpayer runs a profitable business selling potatoes grown on the acre of land adjacent to his home. The taxpayer owns the land and pays property taxes biannually. The expenses for fertilizer are properly deducted on

choices.label: A
choices.text: Schedule A.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Schedule C.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Schedule E.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Schedule F.

questions.explanation:
Cultivating fruit, vegetables, or livestock is considered a farm activity. In this scenario, fertilizer is an ordinary and necessary expense for the potato farm. Farm income and the associated expenses (fertilizer) should be detailed on Schedule F(farm activities are reported on Schedule F). Only the net income or loss from the farm activity is reported on Form 1040; it becomes part of the taxable income calculation.

("Schedule A.") Schedule A is used to report itemized deductions (eg, medical expenses, mortgage interest).

("Schedule C.") Schedule C is used to report the income and expenses from sole proprietorships other than a farming operation.

("Schedule E.") Schedule E is used to report the income and expenses from rental and royalty arrangements, as well as the ordinary income or loss from Schedule K-1s from pass-through activities.

Note:
Income and expenses related to farm activities are reported on Schedule F. The net income or loss from farm operations is reported on Form 1040 and becomes part of the taxable income calculation.
questions.explanationJa: 果物・野菜・家畜の生産は農業活動にあたる。ジャガイモ農場にとって肥料は通常かつ必要な経費であり、農業の収益と費用はSchedule Fに記載し、純損益だけをForm 1040に移す。Schedule Aは項目別控除、Schedule Cは農業以外の個人事業、Schedule Eは賃貸・ロイヤルティやパススルー事業体からの損益を報告する様式である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Individual Taxation Q.10

questions.stem: A calendar-year individual taxpayer uses accrual basis accounting. The taxpayer owns a building that was rented to Mott under a 10-year lease expiring August 31, Year 3. On January 2, Year 1, Mott paid $30,000 as consideration for canceling the lease. On November 1, Year 1, the taxpayer leased the building to Pine under a five-year lease. Pine paid $5,000 rent for each of the two months of November and December, and an additional $5,000 for the last month's rent. What amount of rental income should be reported on the taxpayer's Year 1 income tax return?
questions.explanation:
An amount received for a canceled lease or a rent deposit constitutes taxable income in the year it is received ("$10,000" / "$15,000" / "$40,000").

In this scenario, the taxpayer received a $30,000 lease cancellation payment and a $5,000 advance rent payment (ie, deposit for last month's rent). These two items are taxable when received, as is the revenue earned for November and December. Therefore, the taxpayer should report $45,000 of rental income on the Year 1 tax return
questions.explanationJa: 賃貸借の解約対価や家賃の前払い（最終月分の預り分）は、受領した年に課税所得となる。本問では解約対価$30,000、最終月分の前払家賃$5,000、11月・12月分の家賃$10,000（$5,000×2か月）がいずれも当年に課税されるため、Year 1に報告する賃貸収入は$45,000である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Individual Taxation Q.11

questions.stem: Under a divorce decree settlement, Joan transferred her 50% ownership of their personal residence to Jim. The joint basis of the residence was $200,000. At the time of the transfer, the property's fair market value was $300,000. What was Joan's recognized gain and Jim's basis for the residence?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Joan's recognized gain is $50,000 and Jim's basis is $250,000.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Joan's recognized gain is $50,000 and Jim's basis is $300,000.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Joan has no recognized gain and Jim's basis is $200,000.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Joan has no recognized gain and Jim's basis is $300,000.

questions.explanation:
When taxpayers get divorced, the division of marital assets (a property settlement) is generally a nontaxable event (nontaxable to recipient spouse and nondeductible by payor spouse). Property settlements include any marital assets, such as cash, real estate, vehicles, and investments.

Because the transfer is deemed nontaxable, the adjusted tax basis (not FMV) of the property and the payor spouse's holding period carry over to the recipient spouse. At the time of the transfer, no gain or loss is recognized by either spouse. Instead, any gain or loss is recognized by the recipient spouse using the carryover basis when that spouse sells or disposes of the property.

In this scenario, Joan's adjusted basis for her half of the personal residence was $100,000 ($200,000 joint basis × 50%). Accordingly, Jim's basis of $200,000 in the residence consisted of his one-half interest ($100,000) plus Joan's $100,000 adjusted basis. Because the transfer was nontaxable, Joan recognized no gain or loss at the time of the transfer ("Joan's recognized gain is $50,000 and Jim's basis is $250,000." / "Joan's recognized gain is $50,000 and Jim's basis is $300,000.").

("Joan has no recognized gain and Jim's basis is $300,000.") A basis of $300,000 erroneously uses the property's FMV on the date of the transfer instead of the adjusted tax basis.
questions.explanationJa: 離婚に伴う財産分与は原則として非課税取引であり、いずれの配偶者も譲渡時に損益を認識しない。受け取る側には時価ではなく譲渡側の調整後取得原価と保有期間が引き継がれる。Joanの持分の取得原価は$100,000（共有原価$200,000×50%）で、Jimの取得原価は自分の持分$100,000とJoanから引き継いだ$100,000の合計$200,000となり、Joanの認識利得はない。Jimの取得原価を$300,000とするのは譲渡時の時価を誤って用いた場合である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Individual Taxation Q.12

questions.stem: A taxpayer's spouse dies in August of the current year. Which of the following is the taxpayer's filing status for the current year?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Single.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Qualified widow(er).

choices.label: C
choices.text: Head of household.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Married filing jointly.

questions.explanation: If a married taxpayer dies, the surviving spouse and the decedent are considered married for that entire tax year
questions.explanationJa: 既婚の納税者の一方が死亡した場合、生存配偶者と死亡者はその課税年度全体を通じて婚姻していたものとみなされる。したがって配偶者が8月に死亡した年の申告資格は夫婦合算申告（married filing jointly）となる。適格寡婦（夫）は死亡年の翌年以降に使う申告資格である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Individual Taxation Q.13

questions.stem:
A cash-basis individual taxpayer owns and operates an office building. The taxpayer received the following payments during the current year:

Current rents: $30,000
Advance rents for the next year: 10,000
Security deposits held in a segregated account: 5,000
Lease cancellation payments: 15,000

What amount is included in gross income?
questions.explanation:
The amount included in the taxpayer's gross income is $55,000 ($30,000 in current rents + $10,000 in advance rents + $15,000 in lease cancellation payments).

However, the taxpayer may be required to repay the security deposits, so those deposits are not included in gross income.
questions.explanationJa: 現金主義の場合、当期の家賃$30,000、翌年分の前受家賃$10,000、賃貸借の解約対価$15,000はいずれも受領年の総所得となる。一方、分別管理された敷金は将来返還する可能性があるため総所得に含めない。したがって総所得に含める金額は$55,000（$30,000＋$10,000＋$15,000）である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Individual Taxation Q.14

questions.stem: Gertie owns an apartment building. Out of the rents received each month, she pays herself a management fee. Where should she report her income?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Schedule C only

choices.label: B
choices.text: Schedule E only

choices.label: C
choices.text: Both schedules C & E

choices.label: D
choices.text: None of the above

questions.explanation: Gertie's rental income is reported on Schedule E, as is the deduction for the management fee. Her management fee income is properly reported on Schedule C as business income.
questions.explanationJa: Gertieの賃貸収入とそこから支払う管理報酬の控除はSchedule Eで報告する。一方、Gertie自身が受け取る管理報酬は事業所得としてSchedule Cで報告する。したがってSchedule CとEの両方を用いる。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Individual Taxation Q.15

questions.stem:
A taxpayer, age 45, had the following for Year 1:

W-2 income: $110,000
Traditional IRA contribution: 5,000
Coverdell Education Savings Account contribution: 2,000
Qualifying medical expenses: 12,000

The taxpayer does not participate in any pension or profit-sharing plan other than the traditional IRA. What is the taxpayer's adjusted gross income for Year 1?
questions.explanation:
The taxpayer's AGI is $105,000 ($110,000 W-2 income − $5,000 IRA contribution). Contributions to a traditional IRA are deducted for AGI. No deduction is allowed for contributions to qualified tuition programs (Coverdell education savings plans). Although the medical expenses are limited to $4,125 ($12,000 - 7.5% of $105,000 AGI), itemized deductions are deducted from AGI.

Coverdell education savings:

Previously called an Education IRA, a Coverdell Education Savings Account (ESA) is a trust account set up to pay for qualified educational expenses of the designated beneficiary.
questions.explanationJa: 伝統的IRAへの拠出はAGIを計算する前の控除（for AGI）なので、AGIは$105,000（W-2所得$110,000－IRA拠出$5,000）となる。Coverdell教育貯蓄口座への拠出は控除できない。医療費は控除限度が$4,125（$12,000－$105,000×7.5%）となるが、これは項目別控除としてAGIから差し引くもので、AGIの計算には影響しない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Individual Taxation Q.16

questions.stem:
A taxpayer is a cash basis self-employed air-conditioning repair technician with current year gross business receipts of $20,000. The taxpayer's cash disbursements were as follows:

Air conditioning parts: $ 2,500
Digital advertising: 2,000
Estimated federal income taxes on self-employment income: 1,000
Communication and data services: 400
Charitable contributions: 200

What amount should the taxpayer report as net self-employment income for the current year?
questions.explanation:
A sole proprietorship is a business owned by an individual that is not legally separate from the owner. The business's revenues and expenses are reported on the owner's Schedule C (business's income statement), and the net income or loss is reported on Form 1040. This income is often referred to as net self-employment income.

In calculating the business's net self-employment income, only ordinary and necessary expenses from the business activity are allowed as deductions. In this scenario, those expenses are the parts, the advertising, and the communications. Therefore, the taxpayer should report net self-employment income of $15,100, calculated as follows:

Gross business receipts |  | $20,000
Less allowable expenses:
Air conditioning parts | $2,500
Digital advertising | 2,000
Communication and data services | 400
Total allowable expenses |  | (4,900)
Total net self-employment income |  | $15,100

Although one-half of self-employment taxes can be deducted from gross income to arrive at AGI, estimated federal income taxes are never deductible.

Charitable contributions are personal expenses that are separately deductible, generally as itemized deductions. Therefore, they are not included in net business income calculation.
questions.explanationJa: 個人事業の収支はSchedule Cで報告され、純自営業所得の計算では事業の通常かつ必要な経費だけを差し引ける。本問で該当するのはエアコン部品$2,500、デジタル広告$2,000、通信・データサービス$400の計$4,900で、純自営業所得は$15,100（$20,000－$4,900）となる。連邦所得税の予定納税額は控除できず（AGI計算で控除できるのは自営業税の2分の1）、寄附金は個人的支出として項目別控除の対象となるため事業所得の計算には含めない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Individual Taxation Q.17

questions.stem:
A married taxpayer, age 48, received the following in Year 1:

Interest earned on federal Treasury bills: $ 1,000
Interest earned on municipal bonds: 2,500
Interest earned on state income tax refund: 50
Interest earned on Series EE savings bonds, used to help pay for room and board for dependent in college: 1,500

Given these facts, what total amount from the above should be included in gross income on the taxpayer's Year 1 tax return?
questions.explanation:
Series EE bond interest is excluded if the proceeds are used to pay higher education tuition and fees for the taxpayer, spouse or dependent. The bond must be purchased by the taxpayer or spouse and the buyer must be at least 24 years old. Room and board are not qualified expenses ("$1,050"). Therefore, the taxpayer's gross income is $2,550.

Interest earned on federal Treasury bills | $1,000
Interest earned on state income tax refund | 50
Interest earned on Series EE savings bonds | 1,500
Total | $2,550
questions.explanationJa: Series EE債の利子は、その資金を納税者・配偶者・扶養家族の高等教育の授業料等に充てた場合に非課税となるが、寮費・食費（room and board）は適格費用ではないため本問の$1,500は課税される。地方債の利子$2,500は非課税、財務省短期証券の利子$1,000と州税還付金に付いた利子$50は課税される。したがって総所得に含める金額は$2,550（$1,000＋$50＋$1,500）である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Individual Taxation Q.18

questions.stem: How may taxes paid by an individual to a foreign country be treated?

choices.label: A
choices.text: As an itemized deduction or a credit against federal income taxes due.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Only as a credit against federal income taxes due.

choices.label: C
choices.text: As an adjustment to gross income.

choices.label: D
choices.text: As a nondeductible expense.

questions.explanation: Foreign taxes can either be taken as an itemized deduction or be treated as a credit against federal income taxes due.
questions.explanationJa: 個人が外国に納めた税金は、項目別控除として差し引くか、連邦所得税額から控除する税額控除（外国税額控除）として扱うかを選択できる。税額控除に限定されるわけではなく、AGI計算前の控除や控除不能な支出として扱うものでもない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Individual Taxation Q.19

questions.stem: Which of the following is deductible as a miscellaneous itemized deduction?

choices.label: A
choices.text: An individual's tax return preparation fee.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Gambling expenses to the extent of gambling winnings.

choices.label: C
choices.text: An individual's subscription to professional journals.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Custodial fees for a brokerage account.

questions.explanation: Gambling expenses are deductible as an itemized deduction to the extent of winnings.
questions.explanationJa: ギャンブルの損失（費用）は、ギャンブルの賞金の額を限度として項目別控除に計上できる。一方、個人の申告書作成手数料、専門誌の購読料、証券口座の管理手数料は、現在は停止されている雑項目控除（2%ルールの対象項目）にあたり控除できない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Individual Taxation Q.20

questions.stem: On Oct 1, year 3, Cruz purchased an annuity for $90,000 in post-tax dollars, effective immediately, that pays Cruz $500 a month until death. At the date of purchase Cruz's official life expectancy was 25 years. How much of Cruz's year 3 annuity payments should be included in Cruz's gross income for year 3?
questions.explanation: The amount of a purchases annuity that is excluded from gross income is calculated using a formula that compares the total cost to the total expected return, multiplied by the amount received. At $500 per month, Cruz will receive $6,000 per year or $150,000 over a 25 year life expectancy. With a cost of $90,000, $90,000/$150,000 or 60% of each payment received is excluded from gross income and the remaining 40% is included. In year 3, Cruz received payments in October, November, and December for a total of $500 x 3 or $1,500. Only 40% or $600, would be included in gross income.
questions.explanationJa: 購入した年金の受取額のうち非課税となる部分は、投資額を期待受取総額で割った割合で決まる。Cruzの期待受取総額は$150,000（月$500×12か月×25年）なので、各受取額の60%（$90,000÷$150,000）が非課税、40%が課税となる。Year 3は10月〜12月の3回で$1,500（$500×3）を受け取っているので、総所得に含める金額は$600（$1,500×40%）である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Individual Taxation Q.21

questions.stem: Which of the following is excluded from gross income on an individual's Year 4 tax return?

choices.label: A
choices.text: January Year 5 rent received in December Year 4.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Value arising from personal use of company vehicle in Year 4.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Dividends announced by a C Corporation in December Year 3 and received in January Year 4.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Refundable security deposit received in January Year 4 for a lease ending in July Year 5.

questions.explanation: A refundable security deposit is not deductible at the time it is paid and is not taxable when it is received at the termination of a lease. Rent received in advance is taxable in the period received, not the period to which it applies, making the January Year 5 rent taxable in Year 4. Noncash compensation received from an employer, other than normal employee discounts are taxable to an employee, including the value arising from the use of a company vehicle or other company assets. Dividends are taxable in the period received, Year 4, not the period in which they are declared.
questions.explanationJa: 返還義務のある敷金は、受け取った時点では課税されない。前受家賃は対象期間ではなく受領した期に課税されるため、Year 4の12月に受け取ったYear 5の1月分家賃はYear 4の所得となる。社用車の私的利用による便益は通常の従業員割引以外の現物給与として課税される。配当は宣言時ではなく受領した期（Year 4）に課税される。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Individual Taxation Q.22

questions.stem:
During Year 1, a taxpayer had the following cash receipts:

Wages: $13,000
Interest income from U.S. Treasury obligations: 350
Workers' compensation following a job-related injury: 8,500

What is the total amount that must be included in gross income on the taxpayer's Year 1 income tax return?
questions.explanation:
Wages and interest income from U.S. Treasury obligations are included in gross income. Because interest from U.S. Treasury obligations is received from the federal government (not the state or municipalities), the interest is included in gross income. Alternatively, interest from state or municipal income is specifically excluded from gross income. Awards from bodily injury, such as workers' compensation, are excluded from gross income. The tax law specifically excludes all payments associated with physical injury, including payments for lost wages (workers' compensation).

The total amount included in gross income is $13,350, determined as follows:

Wages: $13,000
Interest income from U.S. Treasury obligations: 350
$13,350:
questions.explanationJa: 賃金と米国財務省証券の利子は総所得に含まれる。財務省証券の利子は連邦政府から受け取るものなので課税され、非課税となるのは州・地方債の利子である。業務上の負傷に伴う労災補償（workers' compensation）は、身体的傷害に関する給付として休業補償分も含めて非課税である。したがって総所得は$13,350（$13,000＋$350）である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Individual Taxation Q.23

questions.stem: Which of the following types of expenses is not an itemized deduction?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Interest expense on a $500,000 mortgage to acquire a personal residence.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Medical expenses greater than 7.5% of adjusted gross income

choices.label: C
choices.text: Charitable contributions of cash and property.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Tax return preparation fees of $1,200.

questions.explanation: Tax return preparation fees, investment expenses, and unreimbursed employee business expenses are currently suspended itemized deductions and cannot be deducted.
questions.explanationJa: 申告書作成手数料は、投資費用や未補填の従業員業務費用と同じく、現在は停止されている項目別控除であり控除できない。$500,000の住宅取得ローンの利子、AGIの7.5%を超える医療費、現金・財産による寄附金はいずれも項目別控除として認められる。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Individual Taxation Q.24

questions.stem:
Which of the following would disqualify a taxpayer from claiming a parent as a dependent?

　Ⅰ.The parent's sole income is tax exempt Social Security income of $25,000. The remainder of the $45,000 it costs to support the parent is provided by the taxpayer.

　Ⅱ.The parent relinquished U.S. citizenship and resides in Mexico on a full-time basis.

choices.label: A
choices.text: I only

choices.label: B
choices.text: II only

choices.label: C
choices.text: Both I and II

choices.label: D
choices.text: Neither I nor II

questions.explanation:
Although a parent is a qualifying relative, to be claimed as a dependent, the individual must be either a citizen of the U.S. or a resident of the U.S., Mexico, or Canada. In addition, the taxpayer must provide over 50% of the total annual support, including tax exempt income like Social Security. As a result, being a resident of Mexico would not disqualify the parent but the parent's Social Security income would.

Regarding the total support -- The parent's total support cost is $45,000. The parent pays $25,000 of that. The child pays the remainder of the $45,000 cost of supporting the parent. That remainder is $20,000. Is $20,000 50% or greater of $45,000? No. $20,000 is only 44.4% of $45,000. Therefore, the taxpayer does not pay 50% or more of the parent's support. The Support test is failed.
questions.explanationJa: 親を扶養家族（qualifying relative）とするには、親が米国市民であるか、米国・メキシコ・カナダの居住者であることが必要なので、米国籍を放棄してもメキシコに居住している点は失格事由にならない。一方、納税者は非課税の社会保障給付も含めた総扶養費の50%超を負担しなければならない。総扶養費$45,000のうち納税者の負担は$20,000（$45,000－親の社会保障給付$25,000）で約44.4%にとどまり、扶養テストを満たさないため、失格となるのはⅠだけである。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Individual Taxation Q.25

questions.stem: A taxpayer borrowed $45,000 secured by land with a basis of $20,000. The taxpayer could not pay the principal, so the bank foreclosed and sold the land for $35,000 as full settlement of the debt. What income should the taxpayer recognize?
questions.explanation:
A cancelled (forgiven) debt is subject to income tax. Recognized income is determined similarly to that from a sale, which equals the value of the benefit received (ie, cancelled debt) minus the adjusted basis of any secured property that was taken (eg, repossessed) from the taxpayer to settle the debt.

Recognized income = forgiven debt − adjusted basis

Therefore, $45,000 - $20,000 = $25,000
questions.explanationJa: 免除された債務は課税対象となり、認識する所得は、担保財産の売却と同様に、免除された債務額からその財産の調整後取得原価を差し引いて計算する。本問では債務$45,000が土地の引渡しで完済扱いとなり、土地の取得原価は$20,000なので、認識する所得は$25,000（$45,000－$20,000）である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Individual Taxation Q.26

questions.stem:
Majors, a candidate for a graduate degree, received the following scholarship awards from the university in 20X2:

$10,000 for tuition, fees, books, and supplies required for courses

$2,000 stipend for research services required by the scholarship

What amount of the scholarship awards should Majors include as taxable income in 20X2?
questions.explanation: A degree candidate can exclude scholarships received for tuition, fees, and required course materials from income. Payments for other expenses and payments that are in exchange for services rendered by the recipient, even if required for the degree, are included in taxable income, so the $2,000 payment for research work by Majors is included in taxable income.
questions.explanationJa: 学位取得を目指す者は、授業料・諸費用および課程で必要な教材費に充てる奨学金を所得から除外できる。一方、それ以外の費用に充てる支給や、学位に必要であっても受給者の役務の対価として支払われる部分は課税所得となる。したがって研究業務の対価である$2,000の奨励金だけが課税所得となる。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Individual Taxation Q.27

questions.stem: Which of the following taxpayers may use the cash method of accounting?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A tax shelter with $10 million in average annual gross receipts.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A qualified personal service corporation with $45 million in average annual gross receipts.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A C corporation with $40 million in average annual gross receipts.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A partnership with a C corporation as a partner and average annual gross receipts of $50 million.

questions.explanation:
C corporations are generally prohibited from using the cash method because it does not clearly reflect income for the period. However, there are exceptions for C corporations and partnerships with a C corporation partner if the C corporation is any of the following:

a small business with average annual gross receipts for the preceding three years that are not greater than an inflation-adjusted amount ($27 million), known as the gross receipts test ("A C corporation with $40 million in average annual gross receipts.")

a farming business

a personal service corporation (PSC)

("A tax shelter with $10 million in average annual gross receipts.") Tax shelters are prohibited from using the cash method and are not eligible for any exceptions.

("A partnership with a C corporation as a partner and average annual gr…") Because partnership income is taxed at the partner level, the accounting method that best reflects the partners' income is used. Partnerships with a C corporation partner cannot use the cash method unless the C corporation meets an exception. Note that the partnership cannot be a tax shelter to be eligible for the exceptions.
questions.explanationJa: C corporationは所得を適切に反映しないため原則として現金主義を使えないが、直前3年平均の総収入が物価調整後の基準額（$27 million）以下の小規模事業者、農業事業、人的役務法人（PSC）は例外として現金主義を使える。適格人的役務法人は総収入$45 millionでも現金主義を使える。総収入$40 millionのC corporationは基準額を超え、タックスシェルターは例外の対象にならず、C corporationをパートナーに持つパートナーシップはそのC corporationが例外に該当しない限り現金主義を使えない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Individual Taxation Q.28

questions.stem: An individual taxpayer wrote a book 2 years ago. The taxpayer continues to receive quarterly payments from the publisher for the right to use the book. This income should be reported on

choices.label: A
choices.text: Schedule B.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Schedule C.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Schedule D.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Schedule E.

questions.explanation:
Form 1040 reports summary rather than detailed information to keep the form a reasonable length. Detailed information is provided on various other forms and schedules submitted with Form 1040. Taxpayers complete only those forms and schedules required to report the details of their activities.

Payments received for the right to use an intangible asset (publish a book = copy rights) or a natural resource are royalties. Royalty income and the associated expenses should be detailed on Schedule E. Only the net income or loss from the royalty activity is reported on Form 1040. Schedule E also is used to report the income and expenses from rental and pass-through activities.

In this scenario, the taxpayer is receiving periodic payments for the right to publish a book. The taxpayer should report this income on Schedule E and the net income or loss from the activity on Form 1040.

("Schedule B.") Schedule B is used to report interest and dividends, not royalties.

("Schedule C.") Schedule C is used to report business activity for sole proprietorships.

("Schedule D.") Schedule D is used to report capital gains and losses.
questions.explanationJa: 無形資産（書籍の著作権）や天然資源の使用権の対価として受け取る支払いはロイヤルティであり、その収益と関連費用はSchedule Eに記載して純損益をForm 1040に移す。Schedule Eは賃貸やパススルー事業体の損益の報告にも使う。Schedule Bは利子・配当、Schedule Cは個人事業、Schedule Dはキャピタルゲイン・ロスを報告する様式である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Individual Taxation Q.29

questions.stem:
Dietz is a passive investor in three activities which have been profitable in previous years. The profit and losses for the current year are as follows:

Gain/(Loss):
Activity X | ($30,000)
Activity Y | ($50,000)
Activity Z | $20,000
Total | ($60,000)

What amount of suspended loss should Dietz allocate to Activity X?
questions.explanation: A suspended loss is the difference between the total loss incurred in passive activities and the amount that may be deducted by offset against income from passive activities. The suspended loss is allocated to those passive activities incurring a loss in proportion to the amounts of losses. The total of the losses is $80,000, offset by a gain of $20,000, resulting in a suspended loss of $60,000. The portion to be allocated to X will be $30,000/$80,000 X $60,000 = $22,500.
questions.explanationJa: 停止損失（suspended loss）は、パッシブ活動の損失合計のうちパッシブ所得と相殺しきれなかった部分であり、損失を出した活動に損失額の比率で配分する。損失合計$80,000（$30,000＋$50,000）からActivity Zの利益$20,000を相殺した$60,000が停止損失となる。Activity Xへの配分額は$22,500（$60,000×$30,000÷$80,000）である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Individual Taxation Q.30

questions.stem:
A married individual received the following in the current year:

Workers' compensation award: $25,000
W-2 wage income: $20,000
Unemployment compensation: $4,800
Damages awarded for medical expenses related to emotional distress as a result of workplace bodily injury: $10,000

What is the taxpayer's current year gross income?
questions.explanation: The taxpayer's gross income is $24,800 ($20,000 W-2 income + $4,800 unemployment compensation). The workers' compensation award and the damages awarded for the medical costs related to emotional stress from a physical injury are excludible.
questions.explanationJa: 総所得はW-2賃金$20,000と失業給付$4,800を合わせた$24,800である。労災補償と、業務上の身体的傷害に起因する精神的苦痛の医療費に対して支払われた損害賠償金は、いずれも総所得から除外される。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Individual Taxation Q.32

questions.stem: A single taxpayer received $155,000 in salary, $15,000 in income from an S corporation in which the taxpayer does not materially participate, and a $35,000 passive loss from a real estate rental activity in which the taxpayer actively participated. What amount of the real estate rental activity loss is deductible?
questions.explanation:
There are two sources of passive income: all rental activities (exception for real estate professionals), and a trade or business in which the taxpayer does not materially participate (partnerships, S corporations). The deduction for passive losses is limited to passive income.

The active participation exception allows a taxpayer who actively participates in a rental real estate activity to deduct up to $25,000 of a passive loss (after offsetting passive income) against ordinary income. The $25,000 deduction is reduced by 50% of modified adjusted gross income (MAGI) over $100,000 and is completely phased out if MAGI exceeds $150,000.

Although the taxpayer meets the requirements for the active participation exception, the deductible passive loss is limited to the $15,000 passive income from the S corporation. The taxpayer's MAGI of $155,000 exceeds the maximum threshold of $150,000, resulting in a complete phase out of the $25,000 additional deduction.
questions.explanationJa: パッシブ所得には、すべての賃貸活動（不動産専門家を除く）と、実質的に関与していない事業（パートナーシップ、S corporation）からの所得がある。パッシブ損失はパッシブ所得の範囲でしか控除できない。賃貸不動産に積極的に関与している場合は、パッシブ所得と相殺した後さらに$25,000まで通常所得と相殺できる特例があるが、MAGIが$100,000を超える部分の50%ずつ減額され、$150,000超では全額消滅する。本問はMAGIが$155,000で特例が使えないため、控除できるのはS corporationのパッシブ所得の範囲の$15,000である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Individual Taxation Q.33

questions.stem: A 22-year-old full-time student earned $11,000 in salary and received $9,000 in interest from corporate bonds. The bonds were a gift from the student's grandparents. The student's parents pay more than half of the student's support, including $25,000 in tuition. Which of the following statements is correct regarding the student's current-year income tax?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The student's salary income and no other income will be subject to the "kiddie tax."

choices.label: B
choices.text: A portion of the student's interest income and no other income will be subject to the "kiddie tax."

choices.label: C
choices.text: Both the student's salary and a portion of the interest income will be subject to the "kiddie tax."

choices.label: D
choices.text: Neither the student's salary nor the interest income will be subject to the "kiddie tax."

questions.explanation:
The kiddie tax was established to prevent wealthy taxpayers from transferring unearned income to family members with lower tax rates (children, grandchildren) to avoid income taxes. The kiddie tax applies to children who meet certain requirements (age, support received) and taxes the child's net unearned income (NUI) at the greater of the parent's tax rate or the child's tax rate.

NUI is calculated as unearned income minus a statutory threshold. Examples of unearned income include interest, dividends, and capital gains.

Because the student (child) in this scenario meets the following requirements, a portion of the student's interest income from the gifted bonds is subject to the kiddie tax.

Student's unearned income ($9,000 interest income) exceeds the statutory threshold ($2,300).

At least one living parent

Age 22 and a full-time student (under 25) with earned income ($11,000 salary) less than 50% of support.
questions.explanationJa: キディ税は、子の純不労所得（不労所得から法定の基準額を差し引いた額）に親と子のいずれか高い税率を適用する制度で、利子・配当・キャピタルゲインなどが不労所得にあたる。本問の学生は、存命の親がいること、24歳以下（25歳未満）の全日制学生で勤労所得（給与$11,000）が扶養費の50%未満であること、不労所得（利子$9,000）が基準額$2,300を超えていることを満たす。したがって贈与された債券の利子の一部がキディ税の対象となり、給与は勤労所得なので対象外である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Individual Taxation Q.34

questions.stem: A taxpayer had AGI of $60,000 in Year 1. During the same year, the taxpayer incurred $10,000 in qualifying unreimbursed medical expenses, all which were charged to a credit card. The taxpayer paid off $7,000 of the credit card charges by December 31 of Year 1. What amount may the taxpayer deduct as an itemized deduction for medical expenses?
questions.explanation:
Cash-basis taxpayers recognize expenses when those expenses are paid by cash or check or when charged to a credit card. Therefore, the date the credit card charge is made, rather than the date the credit card charge is paid off, determines when an item is deductible for tax purposes. If a taxpayer itemizes deductions, only unreimbursed medical expenses exceeding 7.5% of AGI are deductible.

The total medical expenses for year 1 are $10,000 (not $7,000). The expenses are deemed paid on the date of the credit card charge, not when the taxpayer actually pays the credit card company. The taxpayer's itemized deduction for medical expenses is $5,500, calculated as follows: $10,000 expenses deemed paid − $4,500 (7.5% of AGI).
questions.explanationJa: 現金主義の納税者は、費用を現金・小切手で支払った時点だけでなく、クレジットカードで決済した時点でも支出したものとして扱う。したがって控除時期はカード会社への返済日ではなく決済日で判定され、Year 1の医療費は$7,000ではなく$10,000となる。医療費はAGIの7.5%を超える部分が控除対象なので、控除額は$5,500（$10,000－$60,000×7.5%の$4,500）である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Individual Taxation Q.35

questions.stem:
An unmarried taxpayer made the following charitable contributions during the current year:

A cash contribution to a church: $2,000
A donation of used furniture to a hospital's thrift shop, with a fair market value of: 500
A donation to a state university of publicly traded stock purchased by the taxpayer for $3,000 four months ago, with a fair market value of: 4,000

Assuming that the taxpayer's adjusted gross income was $50,000, what amount can the taxpayer claim as an itemized deduction for charitable contributions?
questions.explanation:
The contribution amount is determined by the type of contribution (cash, noncash property). For cash donations, the amount is simply the dollar amount donated. For donations of ordinary income property (stock held for one year or less), the contribution amount is the lower of the ordinary income property's adjusted basis or its FMV.

Because the contributions were made to qualified organizations and the total amount is under the percentage of AGI limitations, the taxpayer can claim a $5,500 charitable contribution deduction.

Cash amount donated: $2,000
FMV of contributed furniture: 500
Appreciated stock held one year or less (ordinary income): 3,000
Total charitable deduction: $5,500
questions.explanationJa: 寄附金の控除額は寄附の種類で決まる。現金はその額、保有1年以下の株式のような通常所得財産は取得原価と時価のいずれか低い額となる。本問は現金$2,000、中古家具の時価$500、保有4か月の株式は取得原価$3,000（時価$4,000より低い）で、AGI基準の上限内に収まるため、控除額は$5,500（$2,000＋$500＋$3,000）である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Individual Taxation Q.36

questions.stem: A taxpayer was the owner and beneficiary of a $200,000 life insurance policy on a parent. The taxpayer sold the policy to a friend for $25,000. The friend paid a total of $40,000 in premiums. Upon the death of the parent, what amount, if any, must the friend include in gross income?
questions.explanation:
Life insurance proceeds generally are not included in the gross income of a beneficiary if the payment is due to the death of the insured. An exception to this rule applies when there has been a transfer of the insurance policy (during the insured's lifetime) for valuable consideration. When this occurs, the policy (1) is treated as an investment, allowing the basis (amount paid) to be recovered tax-free, and (2) a portion of the proceeds is taxable to the beneficiary.

The amount taxable is limited to the excess gross proceeds over the sum of the consideration paid for the transferred policy and subsequent premiums paid on the policy. In this example, the friend (who acquired the policy from the original owner) paid a total of $65,000 ($25,000 for the policy plus $40,000 in subsequent premiums). Of the $200,000 proceeds received, $135,000 ($200,000 − $65,000) is taxable; the $65,000 is treated as a tax-free return of capital ("$0" / "$160,000" / "$200,000").
questions.explanationJa: 死亡による生命保険金は原則として受取人の総所得に含まれないが、被保険者の生存中に有償で保険契約が譲渡された場合は例外となる。この場合、譲受人が支払った対価と以後の保険料は非課税で回収でき、受取保険金がそれを超える部分が課税される。友人の支払総額は$65,000（譲受対価$25,000＋保険料$40,000）なので、保険金$200,000のうち$135,000（$200,000－$65,000）が総所得に含まれる。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Individual Taxation Q.37

questions.stem: An employed, married taxpayer owns three rental properties in which the taxpayer does not actively participate. In the current year, Property 1 had a net loss of $10,000, Property 2 had a net gain of $25,000, and Property 3 had a net loss of $5,000. The taxpayer's W-2 wages were $110,000. Considering only these facts, what is the taxpayer's adjusted gross income?
questions.explanation:
Passive income includes trade or business activities in which the taxpayer does not materially participate (partnerships, S corporations) and all rental activities. Passive activity losses are deductible to the extent of passive activity income. Unused losses are suspended and carried forward to offset future passive income.

There are two exceptions regarding losses from rental real estate activities. The exceptions require that the taxpayer either actively participate in the rental activity or is considered a real estate professional. If neither exception applies, the passive loss deduction is limited to passive income.

Because this taxpayer does not actively participate in the rental real estate activities and is not considered a real estate professional, neither exception applies. Therefore, the losses from the rental activities may offset only passive income. The taxpayer's AGI is $120,000 ( 25000-10000-5000 + 110000)
questions.explanationJa: パッシブ活動にはすべての賃貸活動と、実質的に関与していない事業が含まれ、パッシブ損失はパッシブ所得の範囲でのみ控除でき、残りは停止されて繰り越される。賃貸不動産の特例は積極的関与者か不動産専門家にしか認められず、本問の納税者はいずれにも該当しない。したがって賃貸の損失はパッシブ所得とだけ相殺され、AGIは$120,000（$110,000＋$25,000－$10,000－$5,000）となる。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Individual Taxation Q.38

questions.stem: Mosh, a sole proprietor, uses the cash basis of accounting. At the beginning of the current year, accounts receivable were $25,000. During the year, Mosh collected $100,000 from customers. At the end of the year, accounts receivable were $15,000. What was Mosh's gross taxable income for the current year?
questions.explanation: A cash basis taxpayer will recognize income as it is actually or constructively received. Mosh actually collected $100,000 from customers during the year. The change in receivables is irrelevant to a cash basis taxpayer.
questions.explanationJa: 現金主義の納税者は、所得を現実に受領したか擬制的に受領した時点で認識する。Moshが当年に顧客から現実に回収したのは$100,000であり、売掛金の期首・期末の増減は現金主義の所得計算には関係しない。したがって総所得は$100,000である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Individual Taxation Q.39

questions.stem:
The following information applies to a taxpayer who owns two rental properties, Property A and Property B, and has no other involvement in passive activities:

Year 1 | Year 2 | Year 3
Property A loss | $(14,000) | $(9,000) | $0
Property B income | 5,000 | 3,000 | 0

The taxpayer does not meet the requirements for the rental real estate exceptions. In year 3, Property A is sold to an unrelated party for an $8,000 gain. Other income for year 3 includes $4,000 interest income and $12,000 wages. What is the taxpayer's AGI for year 3?
questions.explanation:
Passive income includes all rental activities unless one of the two exceptions (real estate professionals, active participants) applies. Passive activity losses are deductible to the extent of passive activity income. Unused losses are suspended and carried forward to offset future passive income.

When a taxpayer sells the entire interest in a passive activity, that activity is no longer subject to the passive activity rules. If the activity is sold in a taxable transaction to an unrelated party, the current-year loss (if any) from the activity and suspended losses can offset any active, portfolio, and passive income (including the gain on the sale).

Total suspended loss for two years is 9,000 + 6,000 = 15,000

Gain and other income 8,000 + 4,000 + 12,000 = 24,000

24,000 - 15,000 = 9,000 (The taxpayer reports AGI of $9,000)
questions.explanationJa: パッシブ損失はパッシブ所得の範囲でのみ控除でき、使えなかった損失は停止されて繰り越される。ただし、パッシブ活動の全持分を非関連者に課税取引で売却した場合、その活動の停止損失は売却益を含む能動所得・ポートフォリオ所得・パッシブ所得のすべてと相殺できる。Property Aの停止損失はYear 1が$9,000（$14,000－$5,000）、Year 2が$6,000（$9,000－$3,000）の計$15,000で、Year 3の売却益と他の所得の合計$24,000（$8,000＋$4,000＋$12,000）から差し引くとAGIは$9,000となる。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Individual Taxation Q.40

questions.stem:
A real estate broker reported the following business income and expenses for the current year:

Commission income | $100,000
Expenses:
Auto rentals: 2,000
Referral fees to other (legal under state law): 20,000
Referral fees to nonbrokers (illegal under state law): 8,000
Parking fines: 200

What amount should be reported as net profit on Schedule C, Profit or Loss from Business?
questions.explanation:
Sole proprietors do not file separate tax returns like corporations and partnerships. Instead, sole proprietors report their income and deductible expenses on Form 1040, Schedule C, Profit or Loss from Business. The net income or loss will be reported on the Form 1040 and the owner/operator will pay taxes on the earnings.

For tax purposes, income is income from whatever source derived. Salaries and wages, including commissions (paid to sole proprietors), are included in income when cash or other consideration is received.

Taxpayers are generally allowed to deduct ordinary and necessary expenses incurred in operating their businesses. However, tax policy prohibits subsidizing expenses (through allowing a deduction) that are illegal or relate to bad behavior (parking fines).

In this scenario, the real estate broker should report net profit of $78,000 ($100,000 − $2,000 − $20,000) on Form 1040, Schedule C, Profit or Loss from Business. The illegal referral fees are not deductible ("$69,800" / "$70,000"). Parking fines are government penalties and are also nondeductible ("$77,800").
questions.explanationJa: 個人事業者はSchedule Cで事業の所得と控除可能な費用を報告する。事業の通常かつ必要な費用は控除できるが、違法な支出や駐車違反の罰金のような政府への罰金は控除できない。したがって純利益は$78,000（$100,000－車両賃借料$2,000－合法な紹介料$20,000）となる。違法な紹介料$8,000を差し引くのも、駐車違反の罰金$200を差し引くのも誤りである。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Individual Taxation Q.41

questions.stem: Cole earned $3,000 in wages, incurred $1,000 in unreimbursed employee business expenses, paid $400 as interest on a student loan, and paid $100 in state taxes. What is Cole's adjusted gross income?
questions.explanation: Cole would include the wages in gross income and would be able to deduct the student loan interest (up to a limit of $2,500) to arrive at an AGI of $2,600. The state tax payment is deductible as an itemized deduction (if Cole itemizes) after determining AGI. The unreimbursed employee business expenses are not deductible at all.
questions.explanationJa: Coleは賃金$3,000を総所得に含め、学生ローン利子（上限$2,500）の$400をAGI計算前に控除できるので、AGIは$2,600となる。州税$100は、項目別控除を選んだ場合にAGIを算出した後で控除するものである。未補填の従業員業務費用は一切控除できない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Individual Taxation Q.42

questions.stem: Clark claimed the standard deduction for the year 2 taxable year. In July year 3, Clark received a state income tax refund of $900, plus interest of $10, for overpayment of year 2 state income tax. What amount of the state tax refund and interest is taxable in Clark's year 3 federal income tax return?
questions.explanation: Since Clark did not itemized deductions for year 2, the refund of state income taxes is not taxable in year 3. A refund of state income taxes is only taxable in the year received if the recipient had itemized deductions in the year to which the refund applied. The interest received, however, is not tax exempt and would be taxable regardless of whether or not previously had Clark itemized deductions.
questions.explanationJa: 州所得税の還付金は、還付の対象年度に項目別控除を行っていた場合にのみ受領年に課税される。ClarkはYear 2に標準控除を選んでいたので、還付金$900はYear 3に課税されない。一方、還付に付いた利子は非課税ではないため、過去の控除方法にかかわらず$10が課税される。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Individual Taxation Q.43

questions.stem: Slaton served 10 days on jury duty in year 13, for which Slaton was paid $25 per day by the county. Slaton's employer requires employees to remit to it all pay received by the county during jury duty, because Slaton's employer pays employees their normal compensation for the duration of jury duty. Slaton's W-2 income for year 13 is $40,000. What should Slaton's adjusted gross income be for year 13?
questions.explanation: Slaton will include in gross income both the $40,000 of W-2 income and the $250 earned for jury duty. Since Slaton's employer requires Slaton to remit 100% of the jury duty fees to the employer, the $250 would be an adjustment for adjusted gross income (AGI). As a result, AGI would be $40,000 + $250 - $250 or $40,000.
questions.explanationJa: SlatonはW-2所得$40,000と陪審員手当$250（$25×10日）の両方を総所得に含める。ただし雇用主が陪審員手当の全額の返還を求めているため、返還した$250はAGI計算前の控除（調整項目）となる。したがってAGIは$40,000（$40,000＋$250－$250）である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Individual Taxation Q.44

questions.stem:
An individual taxpayer reports the following information:

U.S. Treasury bond income | $100
Municipal bond income | 200
Rental income | 500
Investment interest expense | 1,000

What amount of investment interest can the taxpayer deduct in the current year?
questions.explanation:
Investment interest expense is interest paid on money borrowed to acquire property held for investment. The deduction for investment interest expense is limited to the lesser of the investment interest paid or Taxable investment income (TII). If the investment interest expense is greater than the TII, the excess expense is carried forward to the next tax year(s).

Note: Rental is passive income.
questions.explanationJa: 投資利子費用は投資目的の財産を取得するための借入金の利子であり、控除額は支払利子と課税対象の投資所得のいずれか少ない額に限られ、超過分は翌年以降に繰り越す。本問の課税投資所得は米国財務省債券の利子$100だけである。地方債の利子は非課税なので含まず、賃貸収入はパッシブ所得なので投資所得に含めない。したがって控除できる投資利子は$100である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Individual Taxation Q.45

questions.stem: An individual paid $5,000 in self-employment taxes throughout the year. What amount is the allowable adjustment to income related to self-employment tax?
questions.explanation:
Self-employment (SE) tax and Federal Insurance Contributions Act (FICA) tax are similar because both levy Social Security and Medicare taxes. However, they are different taxes.

SE tax is imposed on SE income (sole proprietor earnings, guaranteed payments for services from a partnership).

FICA tax is imposed on employee wages.

SE tax is paid 100% by the self-employed individual, whereas FICA tax is split equally between the employee and the employer. The employer can deduct its 50% share of FICA tax as a business expense.

Because a self-employed individual does not have an employer, the individual can deduct (as an adjustment to income) 50% of SE tax when determining adjusted gross income for income tax purposes. However, the 50% of SE tax is not deducted when determining SE income.

In this case, the individual can deduct $2,500 ($5,000 SE tax × 50%) as an adjustment to income when determining adjusted gross income.
questions.explanationJa: 自営業税（SE tax）は社会保障税とメディケア税を自営業所得に課すもので、自営業者が全額を負担する。給与にかかるFICA税は従業員と雇用主が折半し、雇用主は自己負担分を事業費用として控除できる。自営業者には雇用主がいないため、自営業税の50%をAGI計算上の調整項目として控除できる。本問では$2,500（$5,000×50%）である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Individual Taxation Q.46

questions.stem: In Year 5, James Bolton, an individual taxpayer, had ordinary income of $75,000 and incurred net capital losses that amounted to $25,000. During the period from Year 1 through Year 4, Bolton had net capital gains of $2,000 each year. How much capital loss may Bolton carry forward to Year 6?
questions.explanation: An individual may deduct up to $3,000 in net capital losses and the remainder may be carried forward indefinitely. An individual may not, however, carry back a capital loss. As a result, Bolton cannot net the capital loss in Year 5 against the capital gains in Years 1 through 4. Instead, he will deduct $3,000 from his ordinary income in Year 5 and carry forward the remaining $22,000 to Year 6. In Year 6, Bolton will be able to net the $22,000 in losses against any capital gains and/or up to $3,000 in ordinary income. The loss will be carried forward this way until it is used up.
questions.explanationJa: 個人は純キャピタルロスを年$3,000まで通常所得から控除でき、残額は無期限に繰り越せるが、繰り戻しはできない。したがってYear 1〜Year 4の譲渡益とYear 5の損失を通算することはできない。Boltonは$3,000をYear 5に控除し、残りの$22,000（$25,000－$3,000）をYear 6に繰り越す。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Individual Taxation Q.47

questions.stem:
Which of the following education-related expenses can be used to claim an education credit?
Tuition | Fees | Room & Board | Meals

choices.label: A
choices.text: Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes

choices.label: B
choices.text: Yes | Yes | Yes | No

choices.label: C
choices.text: Yes | Yes | No | Yes

choices.label: D
choices.text: Yes | Yes | No | No

questions.explanation: Education credits, which include the American Opportunity Tax Credit and the lifetime learning credit, are associated with tuition and fees paid to qualified educational institutions. They do not take into account amounts paid for room and board or meals.
questions.explanationJa: 教育税額控除（American Opportunity Tax CreditとLifetime Learning Credit）の対象は、適格教育機関に支払った授業料と諸費用である。寮費・食費（room and board）や食事代は対象にならない。したがって授業料と諸費用は対象だが、寮費・食費と食事代は対象外である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Individual Taxation Q.48

questions.stem:
Betty, a salesperson, is an employee with $52,000 AGI who maintains a home office for the convenience of her employer, Smart Systems. The office takes up 5% of Betty's home and is used exclusively for her job. Smart Systems reimburses all of Betty's direct costs of maintaining the home office. Betty also has the following expenses associated with her home:

Expense: Amount
Real property taxes on residence: $3,500
Interest expense on residence: $5,000
Operating expenses on residence: $1,800
Depreciation on residence (based on 5% home office use): $ 150

Considering these facts, how much may Betty deduct from AGI on her tax return, assuming she elects to itemize deductions, as a result of her home office?
questions.explanation:
Miscellaneous itemized deductions subject to 2-percent of AGI limitation have been suspended. These include unreimbursed employee business expenses, non-interest investment expenses, and tax preparation and attorney fees relating to taxable income. Second, when a home office is maintained for the convenience of the employer, the expenses related to that portion of the home are deductible as miscellaneous expenses. This would include 5% of the real property taxes, interest expense, and operating expenses and all of the depreciation on the 5% used as a home office. As a result, total expenses will be 5% x ($3,500 + $5,000 + $1,800) + $150 or $665.

That $665 is what would have been deductible under the prior rules. Because miscellaneous itemized deductions subject to the 2%-of-AGI floor are suspended, Betty may deduct $0 as a result of her home office.
questions.explanationJa: AGIの2%を超える部分を控除できた雑項目控除は現在停止されており、未補填の従業員業務費用もこれに含まれる。従業員が雇用主の都合で自宅に設けた事務所の費用はこの雑項目控除として扱われていたものなので、旧ルールであれば$665（5%×（$3,500＋$5,000＋$1,800）＋減価償却$150）が対象となったが、現在は控除できない。したがって自宅事務所を理由として控除できる額は$0である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Individual Taxation Q.49

questions.stem: Passive activity losses of an individual taxpayer can generally be used to offset

choices.label: A
choices.text: Income from the rental of a residence.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A guaranteed payment received from a partnership.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Dividends income from a foreign corporation.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Interest income on U.S. Treasury notes.

questions.explanation:
A passive activity is any business venture in which the taxpayer does not materially participate. These activities include all limited partnership interests and all rental activities (unless the taxpayer is a real estate professional). General partnership and S Corporation interests qualify as passive if the owner does not meet the material participation tests.

Passive activity losses (PALs) are generally deductible only to the extent of passive gains. The loss rules were enacted to curb the use of tax shelters. In general, rental of a personal residence is treated as any other rental. Since rental activities are generally passive, income from the rental of a residence can be offset by PALs.

("A guaranteed payment received from a partnership.") A guaranteed payment is meant to compensate a partner for services performed for the partnership without regard to partnership income. It is similar to wages or salary and is not considered passive income.

("Dividends income from a foreign corporation." / "Interest income on U.S. Treasury notes.") Dividends and interest are portfolio income, which is not considered passive and cannot be used to offset PALs.
questions.explanationJa: パッシブ活動は納税者が実質的に関与していない事業であり、すべてのリミテッド・パートナーシップ持分とすべての賃貸活動（不動産専門家を除く）が含まれる。パッシブ損失はパッシブ所得の範囲でしか控除できない。住宅の賃貸も他の賃貸と同様にパッシブ活動なので、その所得とパッシブ損失を相殺できる。パートナーシップからの保証支払は役務の対価として給与に類するもの、配当と利子はポートフォリオ所得であり、いずれもパッシブ所得ではない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Individual Taxation Q.50

questions.stem: Taxpayer, a cash basis single taxpayer, reported $50,000 of adjusted gross income last year and claimed itemized deductions of $14,500, including $3,500 of state taxes paid. Taxpayer's itemized deduction amount, which exceeded the standard deduction available to single taxpayers for last year by $1,950, was fully deductible and not subject to any limitations or phase-outs. In the current year, Taxpayer receives a $2,500 state tax refund relating to the prior year. What is the proper treatment of the state tax refund?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Include none of the refund in income in the current year.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Include $1,950 in income in the current year.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Include $2,500 in income in the current year.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Amend the prior-year's return and reduce the claimed itemized deductions for that year.

questions.explanation:
If the standard deduction was used, none of the refund is taxable because no previous deduction for state taxes was taken. If the taxpayer itemized deductions and did not reach the $10,000 state and local tax (SALT) deduction limit, the taxable amount of the refund is the lesser of the refund or the taxpayer's excess itemized deductions over the standard deduction.

Here, the taxpayer itemized deductions but did not reach the SALT limit. Therefore, the includable amount is not the full $2,500 refund ("Include $2,500 in income in the current year."). It is the lesser number, the amount of the taxpayer's itemized deductions that exceeded the standard deduction ($1,950).
questions.explanationJa: 前年に標準控除を使っていれば州税還付金は全く課税されない。前年に項目別控除を行い、州・地方税（SALT）控除の上限$10,000に達していなかった場合は、還付金と、項目別控除額が標準控除額を超えた額のいずれか少ない額が課税される。本問は後者にあたるため、還付金$2,500全額ではなく、標準控除を超えた$1,950を当年の所得に含める。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Individual Taxation Q.51

questions.stem: An individual taxpayer, who is a sole proprietor, owns a specialized truck used to empty portable toilets used by migrant workers on nearby farms. Last year, the taxpayer purchased new gloves and work boots to wear on the job. The taxpayer should deduct the cost of the gloves and boots on

choices.label: A
choices.text: Schedule A

choices.label: B
choices.text: Schedule C.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Schedule F.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Form 1040.

questions.explanation:
A sole proprietorship is a business owned by an individual that is not legally separate from the owner. The owner reports the business's tax activity on their individual tax return. The business's revenues and expenses are reported on Schedule C (business's income statement), and the net income or loss is reported on Form 1040.

In this scenario, the taxpayer's business (sole proprietorship) is not a separate legal entity. Work boots and gloves are ordinary and necessary business expenses for sanitation work. Therefore, the deduction for work clothing is reported on Schedule C. Only the net income or loss from the activity is reported on Form 1040 ("Form 1040.").
questions.explanationJa: 個人事業は所有者と法的に区別されない事業であり、収益と費用はSchedule Cに記載して純損益をForm 1040に移す。作業用の手袋とブーツは仮設トイレ清掃業という事業の通常かつ必要な経費なので、Schedule Cで控除する。Form 1040に記載するのは事業の純損益だけである。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Individual Taxation Q.52

questions.stem: In year 2, Carson was hired as an employee of Barton Co. As part of his employment contract, Barton provided a company car for Carson's spouse, Mary, who is not employed. The value for the use of the automobile in year 2 was $8,000. Carson does not use the automobile. Carson and Mary file separate individual income tax returns. What amounts, if any, should be reported as a taxable fringe value on Carson and Mary's year 2 income tax returns for personal use of the automobile?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Carson $4,000; Mary $4,000.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Carson $0; Mary $0.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Carson $0; Mary $8,000.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Carson $8,000; Mary $0.

questions.explanation:
A fringe benefit is nonmonetary compensation for services performed (employee or contract labor). Unless excluded by law, fringe benefits are taxable to the individual who performed services, regardless of whether the payer provided the benefit directly to the recipient or to another individual (recipient's wife).

Although Mary received the benefit, Carson performed the services that earned the benefit. Therefore, Carson reports the full value of $8,000, and Mary reports $0.
questions.explanationJa: フリンジ・ベネフィットは役務の対価として受け取る非金銭的報酬であり、法律で除外されていない限り、便益を受けたのが本人か他人かにかかわらず、役務を提供した者に課税される。社用車を使ったのは妻のMaryだが、その便益を得る役務を提供したのはCarsonである。したがってCarsonが$8,000全額を報告し、Maryの報告額は$0である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Individual Taxation Q.53

questions.stem:
A taxpayer employed full time as an engineer has the following income items:

Self-employment income | $50,000
Rental income | 15,000
Dividend income | 2,000
Long-term capital gain | 1,500
Short-term capital loss | 1,000

What amount is the taxpayer's passive income?
questions.explanation:
Passive income relates to activities in which the taxpayer is not a material participant (rental income). Portfolio income is derived from investments (dividends, interest, capital gains and losses). Active business income comes from sources in which the taxpayer is a material participant (self-employment income).

Losses from passive activities are deductible only to the extent of passive income. Unused losses are suspended and carried forward to offset future passive income.

Rental income is generally passive unless the taxpayer actively participates in the management of the property. In this scenario, because the taxpayer is a full-time engineer and there is no mention of active rental participation, the rental property is passive income. Dividends, capital gains, and capital losses are portfolio income ("$2,500" / "$17,500" / "$18,500"). Self-employment income is active business income. Therefore, the taxpayer has $15,000 of passive income.
questions.explanationJa: パッシブ所得は納税者が実質的に関与していない活動（賃貸）からの所得、ポートフォリオ所得は配当・利子・キャピタルゲイン（ロス）などの投資からの所得、能動的事業所得は実質的に関与している活動（自営業）からの所得である。本問の納税者はフルタイムの技術者であり、賃貸に積極的に関与している旨の記載もないため、賃貸収入はパッシブ所得となる。配当とキャピタルゲイン・ロスはポートフォリオ所得、自営業所得は能動的所得なので、パッシブ所得は$15,000である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Individual Taxation Q.54

questions.stem:
A taxpayer reported the following items this year:

Net investment income: $4,500
Investment interest expense: 1,400
Fees paid for investment advice: 2,000
Safe deposit box rental fee (used for investments): 300

What amount, if any, may the taxpayer deduct on Schedule A related to investment expenses for the current year?
questions.explanation: This taxpayer may deduct only $1,400 of investment interest as investment expenses. The other $2,300 ($2,000 fees paid for investment advice + $300 safe deposit box rental) of investment expenses is classified as miscellaneous itemized deductions and is nondeductible
questions.explanationJa: Schedule Aで投資関連費用として控除できるのは投資利子費用$1,400だけである（純投資所得$4,500の範囲内）。投資顧問料$2,000と投資用の貸金庫料$300の計$2,300は雑項目控除に分類され、現在は控除できない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Individual Taxation Q.55

questions.stem: A 33-year-old taxpayer withdrew $30,000 (pretax) from a traditional IRA. The taxpayer has a 33% effective tax rate and a 35% marginal tax rate. What is the total tax liability associated with the withdrawal?
questions.explanation: There is a 10% penalty on early withdrawal of retirement funds in addition to the usual marginal rate imposed on income. The total tax rate would be 45% (35% marginal rate + 10% penalty). At 45%, the tax on $30,000 would be $13,500.
questions.explanationJa: 退職年齢前に退職資金を引き出すと、通常の限界税率による課税に加えて10%のペナルティが課される。33歳での伝統的IRAからの引出しなので、適用税率は限界税率35%とペナルティ10%を合わせた45%となる（実効税率33%は用いない）。したがって引出し$30,000に係る税負担は$13,500（$30,000×45%）である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Individual Taxation Q.56

questions.stem: Porter was unemployed for part of the year. Porter received $35,000 of wages, $4,000 from a state unemployment compensation plan, and $2,000 from his former employer's company-paid supplemental unemployment benefit plan. What is the amount of Porter's gross income?
questions.explanation: Porter's gross income ($35,000 in wages + $4,000 in state unemployment compensation + $2,000 in supplemental benefits from the former employer).
questions.explanationJa: 賃金、州の失業給付、元雇用主が費用負担する補足的失業給付（supplemental unemployment benefit）はいずれも総所得に含まれる。したがってPorterの総所得は$41,000（$35,000＋$4,000＋$2,000）である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Individual Taxation Q.57

questions.stem: An individual client asks a CPA to determine whether the client is solvent for federal tax purposes. The client has assets consisting of cash and marketable securities with a basis of $250,000 and a fair market value of $155,000. The client has liabilities of $175,000, which include $130,000 of nondischargeable liabilities under the Bankruptcy Code. Which of the following statements is correct?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The client is insolvent since the client's liabilities exceed the fair market value of the client's assets by $20,000.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The CPA is unable to determine whether the client is solvent or insolvent because the CPA is not an accredited appraiser.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The client is solvent because the fair market value of the client's assets exceeds the client's nondischargeable debt by $25,000.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The client is solvent because the basis of the client's assets totals $250,000 and exceeds the client's liabilities by $75,000.

questions.explanation:
For federal tax purposes, a debtor is insolvent if, immediately prior to discharge, the amount of the debtor's liabilities exceeds the FMV of the debtor's assets. All of the debtor's assets and liabilities are included in the determination, even if they are not included in other legal situations (bankruptcy). In contrast, a debtor is solvent if the FMV of assets held exceeds liabilities owed.

In this scenario, the client (debtor) owes $175,000 of liabilities and holds assets with FMVs totaling $155,000. Because the client's liabilities exceed the FMV of assets, the client is insolvent by $20,000 ($175,000 liabilities − $155,000 asset FMV).

("The CPA is unable to determine whether the client is solvent or insol…") Federal tax law does not require appraisal by an accredited appraiser; therefore, a CPA may determine federal income tax solvency.

("The client is solvent because the fair market value of the client's a…") All liabilities are considered when determining solvency for federal tax purposes. The characterization of debt as dischargeable or nondischargeable relates to bankruptcy laws.

("The client is solvent because the basis of the client's assets totals…") For federal tax purposes, the solvency determination compares asset FMV ($155,000) to liabilities ($175,000), not asset basis ($250,000) to liabilities.
questions.explanationJa: 連邦税法上、債務免除の直前に負債が資産の公正市場価値を上回っていれば債務者は支払不能（insolvent）である。この判定には、破産法上は免責されない負債も含めてすべての資産・負債を含め、資産は取得原価ではなく時価で評価する。本問は負債$175,000が資産の時価$155,000を上回るため、$20,000（$175,000－$155,000）の支払不能である。連邦税法上の判定には公認鑑定人による評価は不要なので、CPAが判定できる。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Individual Taxation Q.58

questions.stem:
During a major sports event, a taxpayer rented his primary residence to spectators for 10 days. The taxpayer's rental income and expenses were as follows:

Rental income | $10,000
Prorated mortgage and taxes | 1,000
Advertising | 500
Commissions | 1,000

How much net rental income must the taxpayer report on the tax return?
questions.explanation:
The treatment of rental income and expenses for a dwelling unit that is also used for personal purposes depends on the number of rental days. If a home is rented for 14 or fewer days during the tax year, the property is considered a personal residence. Homes rented for more than 14 days (significant rental) are considered vacation homes.

For personal residences, rental income is excluded from gross income, and rental expenses (commissions, advertising) are not deductible. Property-related expenses (mortgage interest, real property taxes) are not allocated to rental use.
