In this scenario, the taxpayer's property is a personal residence because it was rented for 10 days. The rental income is excluded from income, and the rental expenses are not deductible. Had the property been rented for more than 14 days, it would be considered a vacation home, and $7,500 of rental income would be taxable ("$7,500").
questions.explanationJa: 私的にも使う住宅の賃貸は、賃貸日数によって扱いが変わる。年14日以下の賃貸であればその住宅は自宅（personal residence）として扱われ、賃貸収入は総所得から除外され、広告費・手数料などの賃貸費用も控除できない。本問は10日間の賃貸なので、報告する純賃貸収入は$0である。14日超の賃貸であれば別荘扱いとなり、$7,500（$10,000－$1,000－$500－$1,000）が課税されていた。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Individual Taxation Q.59

questions.stem:
A taxpayer travels once a month to an out-of-state casino. In Year 4, the taxpayer's expenses and earnings relating to gambling were as follows:

Transportation costs to and from casinos | $1,200
Lodging at casinos | $1,500
Cost of wagers | $20,000
Gambling winnings | $30,000

The taxpayer is not considered a professional gambler. What is the taxpayer's allowed deduction related to gambling for Year 4?
questions.explanation:
Gambling losses are deductible as an itemized deduction to the extent of winnings ("$0"). Gambling winnings are reported separately in income on Form 1040. The gambling losses are not netted against the winnings. Excess losses may not be carried over.

The deduction for expenses associated with gambling also is allowed for any individual taxpayer (not just professionals). These expenses include travel, lodging, and meals. However, the total deduction is limited to the amount of the gambling winnings.

In this scenario, all the expenses are deductible because their total amount is less than the $30,000 in gambling winnings. Therefore, the taxpayer's deduction relating to gambling for Year 4 is $22,700 ($1,200 + $1,500 + $20,000).
questions.explanationJa: ギャンブルの賞金は総所得に計上し、損失はそれと相殺せず、賞金の額を限度として項目別控除に計上する。限度を超えた損失は繰り越せない。出典の解説によれば、ギャンブルに伴う交通費・宿泊費などの費用も、職業ギャンブラーに限らず賞金の範囲内で控除できる。本問の費用合計は賞金$30,000を下回るため全額控除でき、控除額は$22,700（$1,200＋$1,500＋$20,000）である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Individual Taxation Q.60

questions.stem: The income or loss resulting from which of the following activities is most likely to be considered passive?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Annuity income not derived in the ordinary course of a trade or business.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Year-end bonus received by an employee for outstanding performance.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Gain from sale of a trademarked advertising slogan realized by the creator of the slogan.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Income allocated to a silent partner in a general partnership that owns and operates laundromats.

questions.explanation:
There are two sources for passive income: (1) all rental activities (exception for real estate professionals), or (2) a trade or business in which the taxpayer does not materially participate (partnerships, S corporations). Passive income generally includes gains from disposition of an interest or property used in a passive activity. Passive activity losses are only deductible to the extent of passive income (except for rental real estate professionals).

A taxpayer who is a silent partner in a general partnership that owns and operates laundromats is an example of a passive activity from a trade or business in which the taxpayer does not materially participate. Any income or loss received from the partnership is considered passive.

("Annuity income not derived in the ordinary course of a trade or busin…") Annuity income not derived in the ordinary course of a trade or business is classified as portfolio income, not passive income.

("Year-end bonus received by an employee for outstanding performance.") A year-end bonus received by an employee is considered wages, which is active, not passive, income.

("Gain from sale of a trademarked advertising slogan realized by the cr…") If the taxpayer's personal efforts significantly contributed to the creation of intangible property, the income (gain from sale of a trademarked advertising slogan realized by the creator) is considered active, not passive.
questions.explanationJa: パッシブ所得の源泉は、すべての賃貸活動（不動産専門家を除く）と、実質的に関与していない事業（パートナーシップ、S corporation）である。洗濯店を経営するゼネラル・パートナーシップの匿名組合員（silent partner）は、実質的に関与していない事業の典型例なので、その配分所得はパッシブとなる。通常の事業から生じたものでない年金所得はポートフォリオ所得、従業員の賞与は給与として能動的所得である。自ら考案した広告スローガンの商標の売却益も、本人の努力で生み出した無形資産からの所得なので能動的所得となる。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Individual Taxation Q.61

questions.stem: An individual taxpayer received rental income from real estate that was rented below market value to a not-for-profit organization. On what form should the rental income be reported?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Schedule C.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Schedule E.

choices.label: C
choices.text: None since the income was earned from a not-for-profit organization and is tax exempt.

choices.label: D
choices.text: None since rental income is reported as a line item on Form 1040.

questions.explanation:
Only the net income or loss from the rental activity should be reported on Form 1040 ("None since rental income is reported as a line item on Form 1040."). Rental income and associated expenses should be detailed on Schedule E. Schedule E also is used to report income and expenses from royalty and pass-through activities.

("Schedule C.") Schedule C is used to report detailed income and expenses from businesses operated as sole proprietorships.

("None since the income was earned from a not-for-profit organization a…") The rental income is taxable even if the rent is below market and received from a tax-exempt entity. The amount of rent and tax status of the renter are irrelevant. The renter is tax-exempt, not the landlord.
questions.explanationJa: 賃貸収入とそれに関連する費用はSchedule Eに記載し、純損益だけをForm 1040に記載する。家賃が市場価格を下回っていても、借り手が非営利の免税団体であっても、免税となるのは借り手であって貸し手ではないため、賃貸収入は課税される。Schedule Cは個人事業の損益を報告する様式である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Individual Taxation Q.62

questions.stem:
Married taxpayers are filing a joint income tax return. They derive their entire income from the operation of their retail candy shop. Their Year 1 AGI was $50,000. The taxpayers itemized their deductions on Schedule A for Year 1. The following unreimbursed cash expenditures were among those made by the taxpayers during Year 1:

State income tax | $1,200
Self-employment tax | 7,650

What amount should the taxpayers deduct for taxes in their itemized deductions on Schedule A for Year 1?
questions.explanation:
In general, taxpayers who elect to take itemized deductions may deduct certain nonbusiness (personal) taxes on Form 1040, Schedule A. All taxes that qualify as itemized deductions must have been paid during the tax year. Property taxes must be for property located in the U.S. These taxes consist of:

State and local personal property taxes. The tax must be based on the property's value. Standard fees (processing fee) are not deductible

State and local real estate property taxes. The taxpayer must own the property. Deductions for foreign real property taxes are not allowed for 2018 through 2025

State and local income taxes or sales taxes. Taxpayers can elect to deduct one or the other but not both

Foreign income taxes. These can be claimed as a tax credit or a deduction but not both

The deduction for state and local income and property taxes paid is limited to a total of $10,000 ($5,000 for married taxpayers filing separate returns) for 2018 through 2025.

In this scenario, the taxpayers should deduct only the $1,200 state income tax as an itemized deduction on Schedule A for Year 1.

("$3,825" / "$5,025" / "$7,650") All of these choices incorrectly include some or all of the self-employment tax. One-half of self-employment tax qualifies as a deduction from gross income (deducted for calculating AGI) but is not an itemized deduction.
questions.explanationJa: 項目別控除を選んだ納税者は、当年に支払った一定の個人的な税金（州・地方の財産税、州・地方の所得税または売上税、外国所得税など）をSchedule Aで控除できる。州・地方の所得税と財産税の控除は合計$10,000（夫婦個別申告は$5,000）が上限である。本問でSchedule Aに計上するのは州所得税$1,200だけである。自営業税は、その2分の1がAGI計算前の控除となるだけで、項目別控除にはならない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Individual Taxation Q.63

questions.stem: A taxpayer filed an income tax return after the due date but neglected to file an extension form. The return indicated a tax liability of $50,000 and taxes withheld of $45,000. What amount, if any, would be used to compute the penalties for late filing and late payment?
questions.explanation:
A taxpayer who files a late tax return and underpays the taxes due is subject to both penalties--late filing and late payment. Both penalties are calculated as a percentage of the unpaid taxes. The taxpayer paid $45,000 in taxes through withholding. Total taxes due were $50,000. Therefore, the amount of unpaid taxes is $5,000, which is the amount used to calculate both penalties.

("$0") The question indicates a $5,000 underpayment. If the taxpayer had paid all the tax due, or there was an overpayment, then $0 would be correct.

("$45,000") The amount of $45,000 incorrectly assumes the penalties are based on the total taxes paid instead of the total unpaid taxes. Note that withheld taxes are considered paid by the taxpayer even though they aren't remitted with the taxpayer's filed tax return.

("$50,000") The amount of $50,000 incorrectly assumes the penalties are based on the total taxes due instead of the total unpaid taxes.
questions.explanationJa: 期限後申告で納税不足もある場合は、期限後申告と期限後納付の両方のペナルティが課され、いずれも未納税額に対する割合で計算される。源泉徴収された税額は申告書と一緒に納めていなくても納付済みとして扱われる。したがって両ペナルティの計算基礎は未納額の$5,000（税額$50,000－源泉徴収$45,000）である。納付済み税額$45,000や税額全体$50,000を基礎にするのは誤りである。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Individual Taxation Q.64

questions.stem: Alex, a CPA, provided accounting services to a client, Bailey. On December 15, Bailey gave Alex 100 shares of publicly traded stock as compensation for services. The adjusted basis of the stock was $4,000, and its fair market value at the time of transfer was $5,000. On February 15, Alex sold the stock for $7,500. What is the amount that Alex should recognize as gain on the sale of stock?
questions.explanation: when the taxpayer is paid with noncash property, the amount to report as income is the fair market value (FMV) of the property or services received. Alex recognized $5,000 of income when the stock was received. Alex assumed a $5,000 basis in the stock. When the stock was sold, Alex recognized a $2,500 gain ($7,500 − $5,000).
questions.explanationJa: 非金銭的財産で報酬を受け取った場合、その財産の公正市場価値を所得として計上する。Alexは株式の受取時に時価$5,000を所得に計上し、これが株式の取得原価となる（顧客側の取得原価$4,000は関係しない）。したがって売却時に認識する利得は$2,500（$7,500－$5,000）である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Individual Taxation Q.65

questions.stem: Jefferson's investment income consisted of $2,000 in interest from a U.S. Treasury bond and $1,000 interest from a municipal bond. Jefferson also paid $4,000 in investment interest expense. Assuming that Jefferson itemizes, what amount can Jefferson deduct for investment interest expense?
questions.explanation: In this scenario, Jefferson has $2,000 of investment income. The municipal bond interest of $1,000 is tax exempt and thus not included in investment income. There are no investment expenses other than interest. The deduction for investment interest expense ($4,000) is limited to the lesser of TII $2,000 or interest expense ($4,000)
questions.explanationJa: 投資利子費用の控除額は、支払った投資利子と課税対象の投資所得のいずれか少ない額に限られる。米国財務省債券の利子$2,000は投資所得に含まれるが、地方債の利子$1,000は非課税なので投資所得に含まれない。投資利子以外の投資費用はないため、控除額は投資利子$4,000と投資所得$2,000の少ない方の$2,000である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Individual Taxation Q.66

questions.stem: A married couple purchased their principal residence for $300,000. They spent $40,000 on improvements. After living in it for 10 years, the couple sold the home for $650,000 and paid $36,000 in real estate commissions. What gain should the couple recognize on their joint return?
questions.explanation:
Under IRC §121, a married couple filing jointly may exclude up to $500,000 of gain on the sale of a principal residence they owned and used as their principal residence for at least two of the five years before the sale. The couple lived in the home for 10 years.

Amount realized = $650,000 - $36,000 commissions = $614,000
Adjusted basis = $300,000 + $40,000 improvements = $340,000
Realized gain = $614,000 - $340,000 = $274,000
Excluded gain = $274,000 (within the $500,000 limit)
Recognized gain = $0

The $274,000 amount is the realized gain before applying the §121 exclusion.
The $310,000 amount ignores the selling commissions and also fails to apply the exclusion.
The $60,000 amount has no basis in the exclusion rules; the entire gain is within the $500,000 limit for a joint return.
questions.explanationJa:
主たる住居を売却した場合、売却前5年のうち2年以上所有・居住していれば、夫婦合算申告では $500,000 まで譲渡益を非課税にできる（IRC §121）。
実現額 = $650,000 − 手数料 $36,000 = $614,000、取得価額 = $300,000 + 改良費 $40,000 = $340,000、譲渡益 = $274,000。全額が $500,000 の範囲内なので認識する利益は $0。
$274,000 は除外前の譲渡益。$310,000 は手数料を差し引かず除外も適用していない。$60,000 は根拠が無く、利益全額が除外の範囲内にある。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2011 Recently Released Q.12 (AICPA No. 9952)

questions.stem: Doyle has gambling losses totaling $7,000 during the current year. Doyle's adjusted gross income is $60,000, including $3,000 in gambling winnings. Doyle can itemize the deductions. What amount of gambling losses is deductible?
questions.explanation:
Gambling losses are an itemized deduction allowed only to the extent of gambling winnings (IRC §165(d)). For tax years beginning after December 31, 2025, the One Big Beautiful Bill Act limits the deductible amount to 90% of wagering losses, still capped at wagering gains.

90% of losses = $7,000 x 90% = $6,300
Limited to gambling winnings of $3,000
Deductible gambling losses = $3,000

The $0 amount is incorrect because a taxpayer who itemizes may deduct gambling losses up to winnings.
The $5,800 amount has no basis in the gambling loss rules; gambling losses are not subject to an AGI floor.
The $7,000 amount ignores the limitation to gambling winnings.
questions.explanationJa:
ギャンブルの損失は、ギャンブルの所得（勝ち金）の範囲内でのみ項目別控除として控除できる（IRC §165(d)）。2026年以降開始の課税年度は OBBBA により損失の90%が対象となるが、勝ち金を上限とする点は変わらない。
損失の90% = $7,000 × 90% = $6,300、勝ち金 $3,000 が上限 → 控除額 $3,000。
$0 は、項目別控除を選べば勝ち金まで控除できるので誤り。$5,800 には根拠が無い（AGI に連動する足切りは無い）。$7,000 は勝ち金による上限を無視している。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2011 Recently Released Q.15 (AICPA No. 9955)

questions.stem: Sam's year 2 taxable income was $175,000 with a corresponding tax liability of $30,000. For year 3, Sam expects taxable income of $250,000 and a tax liability of $50,000. In order to avoid a penalty for underpayment of estimated tax, what is the minimum amount of year 3 estimated tax payments that Sam can make?
questions.explanation:
To avoid the underpayment of estimated tax penalty (IRC §6654(d)(1)), an individual's required annual payment is the lesser of (1) 90% of the current-year tax or (2) 100% of the prior-year tax. If the prior-year AGI exceeded $150,000, the prior-year percentage is 110% (IRC §6654(d)(1)). Sam's year 2 taxable income was $175,000, so his year 2 AGI was at least $175,000 and exceeded $150,000.

90% of year 3 tax = $50,000 x 90% = $45,000
110% of year 2 tax = $30,000 x 110% = $33,000
Minimum required payments = lesser amount = $33,000

The $30,000 amount uses 100% of the prior-year tax, which applies only when prior-year AGI is $150,000 or less.
The $45,000 amount is 90% of the current-year tax, which is larger than the prior-year safe harbor.
The $50,000 amount is the entire current-year tax.
questions.explanationJa:
予定納税の過少納付ペナルティを避けるには、①当年税額の90% と ②前年税額の100%（前年AGIが $150,000 超なら110%）のいずれか少ない額を納付すればよい（IRC §6654(d)）。前年の課税所得が $175,000 なので前年AGIも $150,000 を超える。
当年税額の90% = $45,000、前年税額の110% = $33,000 → 少ない方の $33,000。
$30,000 は前年税額の100%で、前年AGIが $150,000 以下のときの基準。$45,000 は当年基準で多い方。$50,000 は当年税額の全額。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2011 Recently Released Q.29 (AICPA No. 9969)

questions.stem:
In the current year, a taxpayer reports the following items. The taxpayer materially participates in partnership A.

Salary | $50,000
Income from partnership A | 20,000
Passive activity loss from partnership B | (40,000)

During the year, the taxpayer disposed of the interest in partnership B, which had a suspended loss carryover of $10,000 from prior years. What is the taxpayer's adjusted gross income for the current year?
questions.explanation:
Passive activity losses generally offset only passive income (IRC §469). However, when a taxpayer disposes of the entire interest in a passive activity in a fully taxable transaction, the current-year loss and all suspended losses from that activity are treated as not from a passive activity and may be deducted against nonpassive income (IRC §469(g)).

Salary = $50,000
Income from partnership A (material participation, nonpassive) = $20,000
Current-year loss from partnership B = ($40,000)
Suspended loss from partnership B freed on disposition = ($10,000)
AGI = $50,000 + $20,000 - $40,000 - $10,000 = $20,000

The $30,000 amount deducts the current-year loss but not the $10,000 suspended loss.
The $60,000 amount deducts only the suspended loss.
The $70,000 amount disallows all losses from partnership B, ignoring the release of losses on disposition.
questions.explanationJa:
パッシブ損失は原則としてパッシブ所得とのみ相殺できるが、パッシブ活動の持分全部を課税取引で処分した年は、その活動の当期損失と繰越停止損失の全額を非パッシブ所得から控除できる（IRC §469(g)）。
給与 $50,000 + A（実質的関与・非パッシブ）$20,000 − B 当期損失 $40,000 − 繰越停止損失 $10,000 = AGI $20,000。
$30,000 は繰越停止損失を控除していない。$60,000 は繰越停止損失だけを控除している。$70,000 は B の損失を全く控除していない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2011 Recently Released Q.33 (AICPA No. 9973)

questions.stem:
An individual taxpayer reports the following items for the current year. Partnership A operates a movie theater in which the taxpayer materially participates. Partnership B operates an equipment rental business in which the taxpayer does not materially participate. The building is rented to a third party.

Ordinary income from partnership A | $70,000
Net loss from partnership B | (9,000)
Rental income from building | 7,000
Short-term capital gain from sale of stock | 4,000

What is the taxpayer's adjusted gross income for the year?
questions.explanation:
Under IRC §469, income and losses from passive activities are netted, and a net passive loss is not deductible against nonpassive income. Rental activities are passive by definition (§469(c)(2)), and a trade or business in which the taxpayer does not materially participate is passive (§469(c)(1)). The $25,000 rental real estate allowance (§469(i)) does not apply because the loss comes from an equipment rental business, not rental real estate.

Nonpassive income: movie theater (material participation) = $70,000
Portfolio income: short-term capital gain = $4,000
Passive items: equipment rental loss ($9,000) + building rental income $7,000 = ($2,000) net passive loss, suspended
AGI = $70,000 + $4,000 = $74,000

The $70,000 amount omits the short-term capital gain.
The $72,000 amount deducts the $2,000 net passive loss against nonpassive income.
The $77,000 amount treats the $7,000 of rental income as nonpassive income without netting it against the passive loss.
questions.explanationJa:
パッシブ活動の所得と損失は互いに通算し、通算後のパッシブ損失は非パッシブ所得から控除できない（IRC §469）。賃貸活動は定義上パッシブ（§469(c)(2)）、実質的関与の無い事業もパッシブ（§469(c)(1)）。損失は機器賃貸事業から生じているので、不動産賃貸の $25,000 特例（§469(i)）は使えない。
非パッシブ: 映画館 $70,000、ポートフォリオ: 短期譲渡益 $4,000、パッシブ: 機器賃貸 −$9,000 + 建物賃貸 $7,000 = −$2,000（繰越）。AGI = $70,000 + $4,000 = $74,000。
$70,000 は短期譲渡益を漏らしている。$72,000 は通算後のパッシブ損失 $2,000 を控除している。$77,000 は賃貸収入を非パッシブとして扱っている。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2012 Recently Released Q.11 (AICPA No. 89811)

questions.stem: On February 1, year 1, a taxpayer purchased an option to buy 1,000 shares of XYZ Co. for $200 per share. The taxpayer purchased the option for $50,000, which was to remain in effect for six months. The market declined, and the taxpayer let the option lapse on August 1, year 1. The taxpayer would report which of the following as a capital loss on the year 1 income tax return?

choices.label: A
choices.text: $50,000 long term

choices.label: B
choices.text: $50,000 short term

choices.label: C
choices.text: $150,000 long term

choices.label: D
choices.text: $200,000 short term

questions.explanation:
When an option to buy property expires unexercised, the holder is treated as having sold the option on the date it lapses, and the loss has the same character the underlying stock would have (IRC §1234(a)). Stock is a capital asset, so the loss is a capital loss equal to the $50,000 paid for the option. The holding period runs from February 1 to August 1, year 1, which is not more than one year, so the loss is short term.

The $50,000 long-term amount is incorrect because the option was held only six months.
The $150,000 and $200,000 amounts are based on the value of the underlying shares rather than the taxpayer's investment. The taxpayer never acquired the shares, so the loss is limited to the $50,000 cost of the option.
questions.explanationJa:
購入したオプションを行使せずに失効させた場合、失効日に売却したものとみなされ、損失の性格は原資産（株式）と同じになる（IRC §1234(a)）。株式は資本資産なので、支払ったオプション料 $50,000 がキャピタルロスとなる。保有期間は2月1日〜8月1日の6か月で1年以下なので短期。
$50,000 の長期は保有期間が6か月なので誤り。$150,000 や $200,000 は投資額と関係が無く、株式は取得していないので損失はオプション料に限られる。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2012 Recently Released Q.13 (AICPA No. 89813)

questions.stem: A taxpayer lived in an apartment building and had a two-year lease that began 16 months ago. The taxpayer's landlord wanted to sell the building and offered the taxpayer $10,000 to vacate the apartment immediately. The taxpayer's lease on the apartment was a capital asset but had no tax basis. If the taxpayer accepted the landlord's offer, the gain or loss would be which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: An ordinary gain

choices.label: B
choices.text: A short-term capital loss

choices.label: C
choices.text: A long-term capital gain

choices.label: D
choices.text: A short-term capital gain

questions.explanation:
Amounts received by a lessee for the cancellation of a lease are treated as amounts received in exchange for the lease (IRC §1241). Because the lease is a capital asset in the taxpayer's hands, the payment produces capital gain. The taxpayer has no basis, so the entire $10,000 is gain. The lease was held for 16 months, which is more than one year, so the gain is long term.

An ordinary gain is incorrect because §1241 treats the cancellation payment as a sale or exchange of the capital asset.
A short-term capital loss is incorrect because the taxpayer receives $10,000 with no basis, which is a gain.
A short-term capital gain is incorrect because the holding period exceeds one year.
questions.explanationJa:
賃借人が賃貸借契約の解約の対価として受け取る金額は、賃借権の譲渡の対価とみなされる（IRC §1241）。本問の賃借権は資本資産なのでキャピタルゲインとなり、basis が無いので $10,000 全額が利益。保有期間は16か月で1年超なので長期。
通常所得ではない（§1241 で譲渡として扱う）。basis ゼロで $10,000 を受け取るので損失ではない。保有期間が1年を超えるので短期ではない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2012 Recently Released Q.14 (AICPA No. 89814)

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is correct regarding the deductibility of an individual's medical expenses?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A medical expense paid by credit card is deductible in the year the credit card bill is paid.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A medical expense deduction is allowed for payments made in the current year for medical services received in earlier years.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Medical expenses, net of insurance reimbursements, are disregarded in the alternative minimum tax calculation.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A medical expense deduction is not allowed for Medicare insurance premiums.

questions.explanation:
Medical expenses are deductible in the year paid, regardless of when the services were provided (Treas. Reg. §1.213-1(a)(1)). A payment made this year for medical services received in an earlier year is deductible this year, provided the expenses were not deducted before.

A medical expense charged on a credit card is treated as paid when charged, not when the credit card bill is paid.
Medical expenses are not disregarded for the alternative minimum tax; they are allowed in computing AMTI to the extent they exceed the AGI floor.
Medicare insurance premiums (for example, Medicare Part B premiums) are deductible as medical insurance.
questions.explanationJa:
医療費は、サービスを受けた時期にかかわらず、支払った年に控除する（Treas. Reg. §1.213-1(a)(1)）。過年度に受けた治療の費用を当年に支払えば、（過去に控除していなければ）当年に控除できる。
クレジットカード払いは、カード請求の支払時ではなく、カードで決済した時に支払ったものとされる。AMT の計算でも医療費は AGI 基準額を超える部分が控除でき、無視されるわけではない。Medicare の保険料（Part B など）も医療保険料として控除対象となる。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2012 Recently Released Q.18 (AICPA No. 89818)

questions.stem: Upon her grandfather's death, Jordan inherited 10 shares of Universal Corp. stock that had a fair market value of $5,000. Her grandfather acquired the shares in 1995 for $2,500. Four months after her grandfather's death, Jordan sold all her shares of Universal for $7,500. What was Jordan's recognized gain in the year of sale?

choices.label: A
choices.text: $2,500 long-term capital gain

choices.label: B
choices.text: $2,500 short-term capital gain

choices.label: C
choices.text: $5,000 long-term capital gain

choices.label: D
choices.text: $5,000 short-term capital gain

questions.explanation:
The basis of property acquired from a decedent is generally its fair market value at the date of death (IRC §1014(a)). Property acquired from a decedent is treated as held for more than one year, regardless of how long the heir actually holds it (IRC §1223(9)), so the gain is long term.

Basis = $5,000 fair market value at death
Gain = $7,500 - $5,000 = $2,500 long-term capital gain

A short-term characterization is incorrect because inherited property automatically receives a long-term holding period even though Jordan held the shares only four months.
The $5,000 gain amounts use the grandfather's $2,500 cost as basis; carryover basis does not apply to inherited property.
questions.explanationJa:
相続により取得した資産の basis は、原則として死亡日の時価となる（IRC §1014(a)）。また相続資産は実際の保有期間にかかわらず1年超保有したものとみなされる（§1223(9)）。
basis = $5,000、利益 = $7,500 − $5,000 = $2,500 の長期キャピタルゲイン。
短期とするのは誤りで、保有4か月でも相続資産は長期扱い。$5,000 の利益は祖父の取得価額 $2,500 を引き継いでおり、相続資産には適用されない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2012 Recently Released Q.23 (AICPA No. 89823)

questions.stem: In the current year, Fitz, a single taxpayer, sustained a $48,000 loss on Code Sec. 1244 stock in JJJ Corp., a qualifying small business corporation, and a $20,000 loss on Code Sec. 1244 stock in MMM Corp., another qualifying small business corporation. What is the maximum amount of loss that Fitz can deduct for the current year?

choices.label: A
choices.text: $50,000 capital loss

choices.label: B
choices.text: $68,000 capital loss

choices.label: C
choices.text: $18,000 ordinary loss and $50,000 capital loss

choices.label: D
choices.text: $50,000 ordinary loss and $18,000 capital loss

questions.explanation:
A loss on Section 1244 stock is an ordinary loss, limited in any one year to $50,000 for a single taxpayer ($100,000 on a joint return) (IRC §1244(a), (b)). The limit applies to the aggregate of all §1244 losses for the year, not per corporation. Loss in excess of the limit is a capital loss.

Total §1244 losses = $48,000 + $20,000 = $68,000
Ordinary loss (limit for single taxpayer) = $50,000
Capital loss = $68,000 - $50,000 = $18,000

Treating the losses entirely as capital losses ($50,000 or $68,000 capital loss) ignores the ordinary loss treatment of §1244.
$18,000 ordinary and $50,000 capital reverses the allocation; the first $50,000 is ordinary.
questions.explanationJa:
§1244 株式の損失は通常損失となり、年間の上限は単身者 $50,000（夫婦合算 $100,000）。上限は会社ごとではなく、その年の §1244 損失の合計に適用され、超過分はキャピタルロスとなる（IRC §1244(a)、(b)）。
損失合計 = $48,000 + $20,000 = $68,000、通常損失 $50,000、キャピタルロス $18,000。
全額をキャピタルロスとするものは §1244 の通常損失扱いを無視している。通常損失 $18,000・キャピタルロス $50,000 は配分が逆。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2012 Recently Released Q.25 (AICPA No. 89825)

questions.stem: Johnson worked for ABC Co. and earned a salary of $100,000. Johnson also received, as a fringe benefit, group term-life insurance at twice Johnson's salary. The annual IRS-established uniform cost of insurance is $2.76 per $1,000. What amount must Johnson include in gross income?
questions.explanation:
Under IRC §79, the cost of employer-provided group-term life insurance coverage up to $50,000 is excluded from the employee's gross income. The cost of coverage above $50,000, measured using the IRS uniform premium rates, is included.

Coverage = 2 x $100,000 = $200,000
Excess coverage = $200,000 - $50,000 = $150,000
Included cost = $150,000 / $1,000 x $2.76 = $414
Gross income = $100,000 salary + $414 = $100,414

The $100,000 amount excludes all of the insurance benefit, but only the first $50,000 of coverage is tax-free. The $100,276 amount applies the rate to only $100,000 of coverage. The $100,552 amount applies the rate to the full $200,000 of coverage without the $50,000 exclusion.
questions.explanationJa:
IRC §79により、雇用主負担の団体定期生命保険は保険金額$50,000までの保険料相当額が非課税で、超過部分の保険料相当額（IRSの統一料率で計算）が総所得に算入される。

保険金額 = $100,000 × 2 = $200,000
超過保険金額 = $200,000 − $50,000 = $150,000
算入額 = $150,000 ÷ $1,000 × $2.76 = $414
総所得 = 給与$100,000 + $414 = $100,414

$100,000は保険の便益を全額非課税としており誤り。$100,276は$100,000分の保険にしか料率を適用していない。$100,552は$50,000の非課税枠を控除せず$200,000全額に料率を適用している。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2013 Recently Released Q.6 (AICPA No. 90206)

questions.stem: Which of the following statements regarding an individual's suspended passive activity losses is correct?

choices.label: A
choices.text: $3,000 of suspended losses can be utilized each year against portfolio income.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Suspended losses can be carried forward, but not back, until utilized.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Suspended losses must be carried back three years and forward seven years.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A maximum of 50% of the suspended losses can be used each year when an election is made to forgo the carry-back period.

questions.explanation:
Under IRC §469(b), passive activity losses that are disallowed in the current year are suspended and carried forward indefinitely to offset passive income in future years. There is no carryback. Any remaining suspended losses are fully deductible when the taxpayer disposes of the entire interest in the activity in a fully taxable transaction to an unrelated party (IRC §469(g)).

The $3,000 annual limit applies to net capital losses against ordinary income, not to passive losses, and passive losses cannot offset portfolio income. There is no three-year carryback and seven-year carryforward for passive losses. There is no election to forgo a carryback that allows 50% of suspended losses to be used each year.
questions.explanationJa:
IRC §469(b)により、当期に控除できなかったパッシブ損失は停止され、将来のパッシブ所得と相殺するために無期限に繰り越される。繰戻しはない。活動の持分全体を非関連者に課税取引で処分したときに、残る停止損失は全額控除できる（§469(g)）。

年$3,000の上限は純資本損失を通常所得と相殺する際のもので、パッシブ損失には関係なく、パッシブ損失はポートフォリオ所得と相殺できない。3年繰戻し・7年繰越しという規定はない。繰戻しを放棄すれば毎年50%使えるという選択制度もない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2013 Recently Released Q.17 (AICPA No. 90217)

questions.stem: Smith has an adjusted gross income (AGI) of $120,000 without taking into consideration $40,000 of losses from rental real estate activities. Smith actively participates in the rental real estate activities. What amount of the rental losses may Smith deduct in determining taxable income?
questions.explanation:
Under IRC §469(i), an individual who actively participates in a rental real estate activity may deduct up to $25,000 of rental losses against nonpassive income. The $25,000 allowance is reduced by 50% of the amount by which modified AGI exceeds $100,000 (fully phased out at $150,000).

Excess of AGI over $100,000 = $120,000 - $100,000 = $20,000
Reduction = 50% x $20,000 = $10,000
Allowance = $25,000 - $10,000 = $15,000
Deductible rental loss = lesser of $40,000 loss or $15,000 allowance = $15,000

The $0 amount ignores the active participation allowance. The $20,000 amount is the excess of AGI over $100,000, not the remaining allowance. The $40,000 amount allows the full loss, which exceeds the maximum allowance.
questions.explanationJa:
IRC §469(i)により、賃貸不動産活動に積極的に関与する個人は、賃貸損失を最大$25,000まで非パッシブ所得と相殺できる。この枠は修正AGIが$100,000を超える額の50%だけ減額される（$150,000で消滅）。

AGIの超過額 = $120,000 − $100,000 = $20,000
減額 = 50% × $20,000 = $10,000
控除枠 = $25,000 − $10,000 = $15,000
控除できる賃貸損失 = 損失$40,000と枠$15,000の小さい方 = $15,000

$0は積極的関与の特例を無視している。$20,000はAGIの超過額で、残る控除枠ではない。$40,000は上限を超えて全額を控除している。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2013 Recently Released Q.30 (AICPA No. 90230)

questions.stem:
Individual Lark's year 2 brokerage account statement listed the following capital gains and losses from the sale of stock investments:

Short-term capital gain | $ 6,000
Long-term capital gain | 14,000
Short-term capital loss | 4,000
Long-term capital loss | 8,000

In addition, two stock investments became worthless in year 2. Public Company X stock was purchased in December, year 1, for $5,000, and formal notification was received by Lark on July, year 2, that it was worthless. Private company Section 1244 stock was issued to Lark for $10,000 in January, year 1, and was determined to be worthless in December, year 2. What is Lark's year 2 net capital gain or loss before any capital loss limitation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: $2,000 net capital loss

choices.label: B
choices.text: $3,000 net capital gain

choices.label: C
choices.text: $7,000 net capital loss

choices.label: D
choices.text: $8,000 net capital gain

questions.explanation:
Worthless securities that are capital assets are treated under IRC §165(g)(1) as sold on the last day of the taxable year in which they become worthless. Losses on Section 1244 stock are ordinary losses (up to $50,000, or $100,000 on a joint return) under IRC §1244(a), so they are not part of the capital gain and loss netting.

Net short-term: $6,000 gain - $4,000 loss = $2,000 net short-term gain
Net long-term before worthless stock: $14,000 gain - $8,000 loss = $6,000
Company X stock (bought December, year 1; deemed sold December 31, year 2; held more than one year): $5,000 long-term capital loss
Net long-term: $6,000 - $5,000 = $1,000 net long-term gain
Section 1244 stock $10,000 loss: ordinary loss, excluded from capital netting
Net capital gain = $2,000 + $1,000 = $3,000

The $2,000 net capital loss ($2,000 + $6,000 - $10,000) treats the Section 1244 loss as a capital loss and omits the Company X loss. The $7,000 net capital loss ($3,000 - $10,000) treats the $10,000 Section 1244 loss as a capital loss. The $8,000 net capital gain ($2,000 + $6,000) ignores the $5,000 Company X worthless stock loss.
questions.explanationJa:
資本資産である有価証券が無価値となった場合、IRC §165(g)(1)により無価値となった年の最終日に売却したものとみなす。Section 1244株式の損失は§1244(a)により通常損失（単独$50,000・夫婦合算$100,000まで）となり、資本損益の通算には含めない。

短期: 利得$6,000 − 損失$4,000 = 純短期利得$2,000
長期（無価値株式前）: 利得$14,000 − 損失$8,000 = $6,000
X社株（year 1年12月取得、year 2年12月31日に売却とみなす、保有1年超）: 長期資本損失$5,000
純長期利得 = $6,000 − $5,000 = $1,000
Section 1244株式の損失$10,000: 通常損失で資本損益の通算から除外
純資本利得 = $2,000 + $1,000 = $3,000

$2,000の純損失（$2,000＋$6,000−$10,000）はSection 1244株式の損失を資本損失とし、X社株の損失を落としている。$7,000の純損失（$3,000−$10,000）は$10,000のSection 1244株式損失を資本損失として扱っている。$8,000の純利得（$2,000＋$6,000）はX社株の$5,000の損失を無視している。

questions.stem:
A review of Bearing's year 2 records disclosed the following tax information:

Wages | $18,000
Taxable interest and qualifying dividends | 4,000
Schedule C trucking business net income | 32,000
Rental (loss) from residential property | (35,000)
Limited partnership (loss) | (5,000)

Bearing actively participated in the rental property and was a limited partner in the partnership. Bearing had sufficient amounts at risk for the rental property and the partnership. What is Bearing's year 2 adjusted gross income?
questions.explanation:
Passive losses can generally offset only passive income (IRC §469(a)). A limited partner's interest is treated as passive (IRC §469(h)(2)), and Bearing has no passive income, so the $5,000 limited partnership loss is suspended. Under the IRC §469(i) exception, up to $25,000 of losses from rental real estate in which the taxpayer actively participates can offset nonpassive income; the allowance is not reduced because modified AGI (computed without the passive losses) of $54,000 is below $100,000.

Wages: $18,000
Interest and dividends: + $4,000
Schedule C net income: + $32,000
Income before passive losses = $54,000
Rental loss allowed (limited to $25,000 of the $35,000 loss): - $25,000
Limited partnership loss (suspended): $0
AGI = $29,000

The $14,000 amount deducts the full $35,000 rental loss and the $5,000 partnership loss. The $19,000 amount deducts the full $35,000 rental loss. The $54,000 amount allows none of the rental loss despite active participation.
questions.explanationJa:
パッシブ損失は原則としてパッシブ所得とのみ相殺できる（§469(a)）。リミテッド・パートナーの持分はパッシブとされ（§469(h)(2)）、Bearingにはパッシブ所得がないので、LPの損失$5,000は停止される。§469(i)の特例により、積極的に関与する賃貸不動産の損失は$25,000まで非パッシブ所得と相殺でき、修正AGI（パッシブ損失考慮前）$54,000は$100,000未満なので枠は減額されない。

給与 $18,000
利子・配当 ＋$4,000
Schedule C純利益 ＋$32,000
パッシブ損失前の所得 = $54,000
賃貸損失（$35,000のうち$25,000まで）−$25,000
LP損失（停止）$0
AGI = $29,000

$14,000は賃貸損失$35,000とLP損失$5,000を全額控除している。$19,000は賃貸損失$35,000を全額控除している。$54,000は積極的関与があるのに賃貸損失を一切認めていない。

questions.stem: Baker, an unmarried individual, sold a personal residence, which has an adjusted basis of $70,000, for $165,000. Baker owned and lived in the residence for seven years. Selling expenses were $10,000. Four weeks prior to the sale, Baker paid a handyman $1,000 to paint and fix-up the residence. What is the amount of Baker's recognized gain?
questions.explanation:
Under IRC §121, an unmarried taxpayer who owned and used a home as a principal residence for at least 2 of the 5 years before the sale may exclude up to $250,000 of gain. Baker owned and lived in the home for seven years, so the exclusion applies. Selling expenses reduce the amount realized; fix-up (painting and repair) costs are not deductible or added to basis, but they do not change the result here.

Amount realized = $165,000 - $10,000 selling expenses = $155,000
Realized gain = $155,000 - $70,000 basis = $85,000
Excluded gain (up to $250,000) = $85,000
Recognized gain = $0

The $84,000 amount subtracts the $1,000 fix-up cost and also ignores the exclusion. The $85,000 amount is the realized gain before the §121 exclusion. The $95,000 amount ignores both the selling expenses and the exclusion.
questions.explanationJa:
IRC §121により、売却前5年のうち2年以上所有し主たる住居として使用した住宅を売却した未婚者は、$250,000まで利得を非課税にできる。Bakerは7年間所有・居住しているので適用される。売却費用は譲渡対価から控除する。塗装・修繕費（fix-up費用）は控除もベーシス加算もできないが、本問の結論には影響しない。

譲渡対価 = $165,000 − 売却費用$10,000 = $155,000
実現利得 = $155,000 − ベーシス$70,000 = $85,000
非課税額（$250,000まで）= $85,000
認識利得 = $0

$84,000はfix-up費用$1,000を差し引いたうえ非課税措置を無視している。$85,000は§121適用前の実現利得。$95,000は売却費用と非課税措置の両方を無視している。
