questions.stem: Which of the following statements is correct regarding the deductibility of donations made to qualifying charities by a cash-basis individual taxpayer?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A contemporaneous written acknowledgement is required for donations of $100.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A charitable contribution deduction is not allowed for the value of services rendered to a charity.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A qualified appraisal for real property donations is not required to be attached to the tax return unless the property value exceeds $10,000.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The charitable contribution deduction for long-term appreciated stock is limited to 50% of adjusted gross income.

questions.explanation:
Under Treas. Reg. §1.170A-1(g), no charitable deduction is allowed for the value of a taxpayer's time or services contributed to a charity; only unreimbursed out-of-pocket expenses incurred in rendering the services may be deducted.

A contemporaneous written acknowledgment is required for a single contribution of $250 or more (IRC §170(f)(8)), not $100. A qualified appraisal is required for noncash property (other than certain publicly traded securities) valued over $5,000, and the appraisal must be attached to the return only when the claimed value exceeds $500,000, so a $10,000 threshold is incorrect. The deduction for long-term capital gain property such as appreciated stock contributed to a public charity is generally limited to 30% of AGI (IRC §170(b)(1)), not 50%.
questions.explanationJa:
Treas. Reg. §1.170A-1(g)により、慈善団体に提供した時間や役務の価値は寄附金控除の対象にならない。控除できるのは役務提供に伴って自己負担した実費（未償還分）だけである。

同時期の書面による受領確認が必要なのは1回$250以上の寄附で、$100ではない（§170(f)(8)）。適格鑑定は$5,000超の非現金資産（一部の上場有価証券を除く）に必要で、鑑定書の添付が求められるのは評価額が$500,000を超える場合なので、$10,000という基準は誤り。値上がりした長期保有株式など長期キャピタルゲイン資産の公益慈善団体への寄附は原則AGIの30%が上限で、50%ではない（§170(b)(1)）。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2014 Recently Released Q.13 (AICPA No. 90563)

questions.stem: Nan, a cash basis taxpayer, borrowed money from a bank and signed a 10 year interest-bearing note on business property on January 1 of the current year. The cash flow from Nan's business enabled Nan to prepay the first three years of interest attributable to the note on December 31 of the current year. How should Nan treat the prepayment of interest for tax purposes?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Deduct the entire amount as a current expense

choices.label: B
choices.text: Deduct the current year’s interest and amortize the balance over the next two years

choices.label: C
choices.text: Capitalize the interest and amortize the balance over the 10-year loan period

choices.label: D
choices.text: Capitalize the interest as part of the basis of the business property

questions.explanation:
Under IRC §461(g)(1), a cash-basis taxpayer who prepays interest must treat the prepaid interest as paid in the period to which it is allocable, as if the taxpayer used the accrual method. Nan may deduct only the interest attributable to the current year; the interest prepaid for the next two years is deducted in those years.

Deducting the entire three years of interest currently is not permitted because §461(g) overrides the normal cash-method rule for prepaid interest. Amortizing over the 10-year loan period spreads the interest over years to which it does not relate; the prepayment covers only three years. Interest on a loan is not added to the basis of business property merely because the loan is secured by that property.
questions.explanationJa:
IRC §461(g)(1)により、現金主義の納税者が前払いした利息は、発生主義と同様に、その利息が帰属する期間に支払ったものとして扱われる。Nanが当年に控除できるのは当年分の利息だけで、翌年以降2年分の前払利息はそれぞれの年に控除する。

3年分を一括で当年控除することは、§461(g)が前払利息について現金主義の通常ルールに優先するため認められない。10年のローン期間で償却するのは、前払いが3年分にすぎないのに関係のない年に配分しており誤り。事業用資産を担保とする借入れの利息だからといって、その資産のベーシスに加算されるわけではない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2014 Recently Released Q.27 (AICPA No. 90577)

questions.stem: The Jacksons, who file a joint return, actively participate in a solely-owned rental real estate activity that produces a $30,000 loss during the current year. Their adjusted gross income was $120,000 before considering the rental activity. How much of the rental loss, if any, are the Jacksons entitled to deduct?
questions.explanation:
Under IRC §469(i), an individual who actively participates in a rental real estate activity may deduct up to $25,000 of rental losses against nonpassive income. The $25,000 allowance is reduced by 50% of modified AGI over $100,000 (fully phased out at $150,000).

Allowance before phase-out: $25,000
Reduction: ($120,000 − $100,000) × 50% = $10,000
Allowable loss: $25,000 − $10,000 = $15,000

The remaining $15,000 of the $30,000 loss is suspended and carried forward as a passive loss.

The $0 amount ignores the active-participation exception. The $25,000 amount ignores the AGI phase-out. The $30,000 amount allows the entire loss, but the special allowance is capped at $25,000 before the phase-out.
questions.explanationJa:
IRC §469(i)により、賃貸不動産に積極的に関与（active participation）する個人は、賃貸損失を最大$25,000まで他の所得と通算できる。この枠は修正AGIが$100,000を超える部分の50%だけ縮小する（$150,000で消滅）。

縮小前の枠: $25,000
縮小額: ($120,000 − $100,000) × 50% = $10,000
控除可能額: $25,000 − $10,000 = $15,000

$30,000の損失のうち残り$15,000はパッシブ損失として繰り越される。

$0は積極的関与の特例を無視している。$25,000はAGIによる縮小を無視している。$30,000は損失全額を認めているが、特例枠は縮小前でも$25,000が上限である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2014 Recently Released Q.32 (AICPA No. 90582)

questions.stem:
As a result of a divorce, a taxpayer received the following during the current year:

Cash from the property settlement | $100,000
Child support | 12,000
Alimony payments | 30,000

What amount, if any, must be included in gross income for the current year?
questions.explanation:
The question treats the amounts as received in the current year as a result of a divorce, so the divorce instrument is treated as executed after December 31, 2018. For such instruments, the TCJA repealed the inclusion of alimony in the recipient's gross income (former IRC §71) and the payer's deduction (former §215). Alimony received is therefore excluded.

Cash from the property settlement: excluded (transfer between spouses incident to divorce, IRC §1041) → $0
Child support: never included in the recipient's income → $0
Alimony payments: excluded for post-2018 divorce instruments → $0
Total gross income: $0

The $30,000 amount applies the pre-2019 rule that included alimony in income. The $130,000 amount also includes the property settlement, and the $142,000 amount includes all three items, including child support.
questions.explanationJa:
問題は当年に離婚に伴って受け取った金額を扱っているので、離婚証書は2018年12月31日より後に作成されたものとして扱う。TCJAにより、2019年以降の離婚証書に基づく扶養料（alimony）は受取側の総所得に含まれず（旧IRC §71）、支払側も控除できない（旧§215）。

財産分与の現金: 離婚に伴う配偶者間の移転として非課税（IRC §1041）→ $0
子の養育費: 受取側の所得にならない → $0
扶養料: 2019年以降の離婚証書では非課税 → $0
総所得算入額: $0

$30,000は扶養料を所得に含めていた2018年以前の規定を当てはめている。$130,000はさらに財産分与を含め、$142,000は養育費まで含めている。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2015 Recently Released Q.12 (AICPA No. 90812)

questions.stem: Thompson's spouse died in year 1. Thompson did not remarry in year 2 and lived alone the entire year. What is Thompson's year 2 filing status?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Married filing jointly

choices.label: B
choices.text: Surviving spouse

choices.label: C
choices.text: Head of household

choices.label: D
choices.text: Single

questions.explanation:
A taxpayer whose spouse died in year 1 may file a joint return for year 1 (the year of death). In year 2, a joint return is no longer available because Thompson is not married. Surviving spouse (qualifying widow(er)) status for the two years after the year of death requires maintaining a household for a dependent child (IRC §2(a)), and head of household status requires maintaining a household for a qualifying person (IRC §2(b)). Thompson lived alone the entire year 2, so neither applies, and Thompson files as single.

Married filing jointly applies only for the year of the spouse's death. Surviving spouse and head of household both require a qualifying child or other qualifying person living in the home, which Thompson does not have.
questions.explanationJa:
配偶者が1年目に死亡した場合、死亡年である1年目は夫婦合算申告ができる。2年目は婚姻状態ではないため合算申告はできない。死亡年の翌2年間に使える適格寡婦（夫）（surviving spouse）は扶養する子と同居する世帯の維持が条件（IRC §2(a)）で、世帯主（head of household）も適格者のための世帯の維持が条件（IRC §2(b)）である。Thompsonは2年目に一人暮らしなので、どちらにも当たらず独身（single）となる。

夫婦合算申告は配偶者の死亡年に限られる。適格寡婦（夫）と世帯主は、いずれも同居する扶養の子や適格者が必要で、Thompsonには該当者がいない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2015 Recently Released Q.13 (AICPA No. 90813)

questions.stem: Logan, an employee of Argon Industries, earned a salary of $60,000 in year 2. In addition, the following two transactions between Logan and Argon occurred in year 2: Logan received a bonus of 100 shares of publicly-traded stock worth $13,000 with a basis to Argon of $8,000, and Logan purchased 1,000 shares of unrestricted Argon stock pursuant to a nonqualifying stock option plan for $10 per share when stock was valued at $25 per share. What amount of compensation should Argon report in Logan's Form W-2 for year 2?
questions.explanation:
Compensation reported on Form W-2 includes cash wages and the fair market value of property transferred to the employee for services. When an employee exercises a nonqualified stock option that has no readily ascertainable fair market value at grant, the spread at exercise (fair market value less the exercise price) is compensation (Treas. Reg. §1.83-7).

Salary: $60,000
Stock bonus at fair market value: $13,000
Nonqualified option spread: 1,000 shares × ($25 − $10) = $15,000
Total W-2 compensation: $60,000 + $13,000 + $15,000 = $88,000

Argon's $8,000 basis in the bonus shares affects Argon's own gain on transferring the shares, not the amount of Logan's compensation. The $60,000 amount omits both stock items. The $73,000 amount omits the option spread. The $93,000 amount overstates the stock-related income; only the $13,000 fair market value of the bonus shares and the $15,000 option spread are compensation.
questions.explanationJa:
W-2に記載する報酬には、現金給与に加え、役務の対価として従業員に移転した資産の時価が含まれる。付与時に時価が容易に算定できない非適格ストックオプションを行使した場合、行使時の時価と行使価格の差額が報酬になる（Treas. Reg. §1.83-7）。

給与: $60,000
賞与として受けた株式の時価: $13,000
非適格オプションの差額: 1,000株 × ($25 − $10) = $15,000
W-2報酬合計: $60,000 + $13,000 + $15,000 = $88,000

賞与株式のArgon側の取得価額$8,000は、Argonが株式を移転したときの利得に関係するだけで、Loganの報酬額には影響しない。$60,000は株式関連の2項目を落としている。$73,000はオプションの差額を落としている。$93,000は株式関連の所得を過大にしており、報酬になるのは賞与株式の時価$13,000とオプションの差額$15,000だけである。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2015 Recently Released Q.33 (AICPA No. 90833)

questions.stem: Flowers, a married taxpayer, purchased an annuity for $64,400 that will pay $700 per month over the life of Flowers and Flowers' spouse. At the time of purchase the couple's joint life expectancy was 23 years. Flowers received payment beginning April 1, year 1 amounting to $6,300 in the first year of the annuity contract. How much is includible in Flowers' gross income in the first year?
questions.explanation:
Under IRC §72(b), each annuity payment is excluded from gross income in the ratio of the investment in the contract to the expected return under the contract.

Expected return: $700 × 12 months × 23 years = $193,200
Exclusion ratio: $64,400 ÷ $193,200 = 1/3
Payments received in year 1: $6,300 (9 payments of $700)
Excluded portion: $6,300 × 1/3 = $2,100
Includible in gross income: $6,300 − $2,100 = $4,200

The $0 amount treats all payments as a return of investment. The $2,100 amount is the excluded portion, not the taxable portion. The $6,300 amount ignores the recovery of the $64,400 investment.
questions.explanationJa:
IRC §72(b)により、年金の各受取額のうち、投資額（払込額）÷期待受取総額の割合だけが総所得から除外される。

期待受取総額: $700 × 12か月 × 23年 = $193,200
除外割合: $64,400 ÷ $193,200 = 1/3
1年目の受取額: $6,300（$700 × 9回）
除外額: $6,300 × 1/3 = $2,100
総所得算入額: $6,300 − $2,100 = $4,200

$0は受取額全額を投資の回収としている。$2,100は除外額であり課税部分ではない。$6,300は投資額$64,400の回収を無視している。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2015 Recently Released Q.34 (AICPA No. 90834)

questions.stem: Which of the following statements about the alternative minimum tax (AMT) of an individual is correct?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It is determined from the tax rate schedules and computed on income that exceeds $100,000.

choices.label: B
choices.text: It is computed on an individual's regular taxable income at a rate of 28%.

choices.label: C
choices.text: It is calculated after certain tax preference items that may be used as an alternative to the regular tax are deducted.

choices.label: D
choices.text: AMT credits may be carried forward to future tax years.

questions.explanation:
Under IRC §53, the minimum tax credit for AMT paid that is attributable to deferral items (timing differences) is carried forward indefinitely and may offset regular tax in future years to the extent regular tax exceeds tentative minimum tax. AMT credits may therefore be carried forward.

The AMT is not computed by applying the regular tax rate schedules to income over $100,000; it is computed by applying the AMT rates of 26% and 28% (§55(b)) to alternative minimum taxable income after the AMT exemption. It is not computed on regular taxable income at a flat 28% rate, because regular taxable income must first be increased by adjustments and preferences to arrive at AMTI. Tax preference items are added back to taxable income, not deducted.
questions.explanationJa:
IRC §53により、繰延項目（タイミング差異）に起因して納付したAMTは最低税額控除（minimum tax credit）として無期限に繰り越し、将来の年度に通常の税額が仮最低税額を超える範囲で通常の税額から控除できる。したがってAMTクレジットは繰越可能である。

AMTは$100,000超の所得に通常の税率表を当てはめて計算するものではなく、AMT控除後の代替最低課税所得（AMTI）に26%・28%のAMT税率（§55(b)）を適用して計算する。通常の課税所得にそのまま28%を掛けるのでもなく、まず調整項目・優遇項目を加減してAMTIを求める。優遇項目は課税所得に加算するもので、控除するものではない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2016 Recently Released Q.31 (AICPA No. null)

questions.stem:
Jensen reported the following items during the current year:

Fair rent value of employer-owned condominium | $ 1,400
Cash found in a $30 flea-market desk | 400
Inheritance | 11,000

The employer allowed Jensen to use the condominium for free in recognition of outstanding achievement.
Based on this information, what is Jensen's gross income for the year?
questions.explanation:
Gross income includes all income from whatever source derived (IRC §61). The free use of the employer's condominium is compensation for services, and its fair rental value ($1,400) is taxable; it is not an excludable employee achievement award, which must be tangible personal property under §274(j). Cash found in the desk is treasure trove and is income when reduced to undisputed possession (Treas. Reg. §1.61-14(a)), so the full $400 is included. An inheritance is excluded under §102(a).

Gross income = $1,400 + $400 = $1,800

The $1,400 amount omits the found cash. The $1,770 amount reduces the found cash by the $30 desk price, but the $30 is the cost of the desk, not an offset against the cash found. The $12,400 amount includes the excludable $11,000 inheritance and omits the found cash.
questions.explanationJa:
総所得にはあらゆる源泉からの所得が含まれる（IRC §61）。雇用主のコンドミニアムの無償使用は役務の対価であり、公正賃料$1,400は課税される。従業員功労賞の除外は有形動産に限られる（§274(j)）ため該当しない。机から見つけた現金は埋蔵物（treasure trove）として、争いなく占有した時点で所得となる（Treas. Reg. §1.61-14(a)）ので$400全額を含める。相続は§102(a)で除外される。

総所得 = $1,400 + $400 = $1,800

$1,400は見つけた現金を漏らしている。$1,770は現金から机の代金$30を差し引いているが、$30は机の取得費であり現金の所得を減らさない。$12,400は除外される相続$11,000を含め、見つけた現金を漏らしている。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2017 Recently Released Q.10 (AICPA No. null)

questions.stem:
Dr. Merry, a self-employed dentist, incurred the following expenses:

Investment expenses | $700
Custodial fees for Dr. Merry's Keogh plan | 40
Work uniforms for Dr. Merry and employees | 320
Periodicals for the waiting room | 110
Dental education seminar | 1,300

What is the amount of expenses the doctor can deduct as business expenses on Schedule C, Profit or Loss from Business?
questions.explanation:
Schedule C deductions are ordinary and necessary expenses of the taxpayer's trade or business (IRC §162). Work uniforms not suitable for ordinary wear ($320), periodicals for patients in the reception area ($110), and a dental education seminar that maintains or improves the dentist's skills ($1,300) are business expenses.

Schedule C deductions = $320 + $110 + $1,300 = $1,730

Investment expenses ($700) relate to producing investment income under §212, not to the dental practice, and are not Schedule C expenses. Custodial fees for the dentist's own Keogh plan ($40) relate to the owner's personal retirement account, not to operating the business. The $1,770 amount adds the Keogh fees, and the $2,430 amount adds the investment expenses. The $1,620 amount omits the $110 of reception-area periodicals.
questions.explanationJa:
Schedule Cで控除できるのは、事業に通常かつ必要な経費である（IRC §162）。普段着に適さない仕事用の制服$320、待合室用の定期刊行物$110、歯科医としての技能を維持・向上させる研修$1,300は事業経費である。

Schedule Cの控除額 = $320 + $110 + $1,300 = $1,730

投資費用$700は§212の投資所得に関するもので、歯科業務の経費ではない。本人のKeoghプランの管理手数料$40は本人の退職口座に関するもので、事業運営の経費ではない。$1,770はKeogh手数料を、$2,430は投資費用を加えた額で、$1,620は待合室の定期刊行物$110を漏らした額である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2017 Recently Released Q.11 (AICPA No. null)

questions.stem: The term active participation for a passive activity loss is relevant in relation to

choices.label: A
choices.text: Rental real estate activities.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Working interests in oil and gas properties.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Passive activities in which the taxpayer materially participates.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Passive activities in which the taxpayer does not materially participate.

questions.explanation:
Under IRC §469(i), an individual who actively participates in a rental real estate activity may deduct up to $25,000 of passive losses from that activity against nonpassive income, phased out as modified AGI rises from $100,000 to $150,000. Active participation is a lower standard than material participation (for example, making management decisions such as approving tenants and setting rents).

Working interests in oil and gas properties are excluded from the passive activity rules by §469(c)(3) regardless of participation. Activities in which the taxpayer materially participates are not passive, and for activities in which the taxpayer does not materially participate the relevant concept is material participation, not active participation.
questions.explanationJa:
IRC §469(i)により、賃貸不動産活動に積極的に関与（active participation）する個人は、その活動のパッシブ損失のうち最大$25,000を非パッシブ所得と通算できる（修正AGI $100,000〜$150,000で段階的に縮小）。積極的関与は、入居者の承認や賃料設定などの経営判断への関与で足り、実質的関与（material participation）より緩い基準である。

石油・ガスの作業権益（working interest）は関与の程度にかかわらずパッシブ活動から除外される（§469(c)(3)）。実質的に関与している活動はそもそもパッシブではなく、実質的に関与していない活動で問題となるのは実質的関与の有無であり、積極的関与ではない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2017 Recently Released Q.12 (AICPA No. null)

questions.stem: Sanderson has made deductible contributions to his traditional IRA for many years. Sanderson recently retired at age 60 and received a distribution of $150,000. In which way, if any, will the distribution be taxed?

choices.label: A
choices.text: As a capital gain.

choices.label: B
choices.text: As ordinary income.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Subject to a 10% penalty.

choices.label: D
choices.text: It will not be taxed.

questions.explanation:
Distributions from a traditional IRA are included in gross income as ordinary income under IRC §408(d)(1) and §72, to the extent they exceed any nondeductible contributions (basis). Because all of Sanderson's contributions were deductible, he has no basis and the entire $150,000 is ordinary income.

IRA distributions are not capital gains, even if the account held capital assets. The 10% additional tax on early distributions under §72(t) does not apply because Sanderson is over age 59½. The distribution is not tax-free; only qualified distributions from a Roth IRA are excluded.
questions.explanationJa:
従来型IRAからの分配は、控除されなかった拠出額（basis）を超える部分が通常所得として総所得に算入される（IRC §408(d)(1)、§72）。Sandersonの拠出はすべて控除済みなのでbasisはなく、$150,000全額が通常所得となる。

IRA内で資本資産を運用していてもIRAの分配はキャピタルゲインにならない。60歳であり59½歳を超えているので、§72(t)の早期分配に対する10%の追加税はかからない。非課税となるのはRoth IRAの適格分配のみであり、本問の分配は課税される。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2017 Recently Released Q.30 (AICPA No. null)

questions.stem: Which of the following would qualify as a deductible charitable contribution in year 1 for an individual taxpayer?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A $200 contribution to the taxpayer's church charged by credit card on December 31, year 1.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A $450 contribution to a senator's campaign on December 31, year 1.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A $1,000 contribution to a foreign charity on December 31, year 1.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A contribution on December 31, year 1, of $500 worth of clothing to the Salvation Army for which substantiation was not obtained.

questions.explanation:
A charitable contribution charged to a credit card is treated as paid in the year it is charged, even though the card balance is paid later (Rev. Rul. 78-38). A church is a qualified organization under IRC §170(c)(2), so the $200 charged on December 31 of year 1 is deductible in year 1.

Contributions to a political campaign are not made to a §170(c) organization and are not deductible. Contributions to a foreign charity are not deductible because §170(c)(2) requires the organization to be created or organized in the United States. A noncash contribution of $250 or more, such as the $500 of clothing, requires a contemporaneous written acknowledgment from the donee under §170(f)(8); without that substantiation no deduction is allowed.
questions.explanationJa:
クレジットカードで支払った寄附は、カード代金を後で支払う場合でもカードで決済した年に支払ったものとされる（Rev. Rul. 78-38）。教会はIRC §170(c)(2)の適格団体なので、year 1の12月31日にカード決済した$200はyear 1に控除できる。

選挙運動への献金は§170(c)の団体への寄附ではないので控除できない。外国の慈善団体への寄附は、§170(c)(2)が米国で設立された団体であることを求めているため控除できない。$250以上の現物寄附（$500の衣類）は§170(f)(8)により受贈団体の書面による受領証明が必要で、それがなければ控除は認められない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2017 Recently Released Q.31 (AICPA No. null)

questions.stem: Bartlet owns a manufacturing business and participates in the business. Which of the following conditions would cause the business to be considered a nonpassive activity for Bartlet?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Bartlet participates in the business for more than 500 hours during a year.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The business made a profit in any three of the last five years that preceded the current year.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The business has at least 10 employees who, individually or collectively, work for the business more than 1,000 hours in a year.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Bartlet files an election with the IRS postponing nonpassive activity classification.

questions.explanation:
A trade or business is a nonpassive activity for a taxpayer who materially participates in it (IRC §469(c)(1), (h)(1)). Under Treas. Reg. §1.469-5T(a)(1), an individual materially participates if the individual participates in the activity for more than 500 hours during the year.

Having a profit in three of the last five years is the §183(d) presumption that an activity is engaged in for profit (hobby loss rules), not a material participation test. Hours worked by employees do not count toward the owner's participation. There is no election to postpone or choose nonpassive classification; status depends on the taxpayer's own participation.
questions.explanationJa:
納税者が実質的に関与（material participation）している事業は非パッシブ活動となる（IRC §469(c)(1)、(h)(1)）。Treas. Reg. §1.469-5T(a)(1)では、個人がその年に500時間を超えて活動に参加していれば実質的関与に当たる。

過去5年のうち3年で利益が出ていることは、§183(d)の営利目的の推定（趣味損失のルール）であり、実質的関与の基準ではない。従業員の作業時間は所有者の関与時間に算入されない。非パッシブとする区分を延期・選択する届出制度もなく、本人の関与で判断される。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2017 Recently Released Q.32 (AICPA No. null)

questions.stem: Juan recently started operating a flower shop as a proprietorship. In its first year of operations, the shop had a taxable income of $60,000. Assuming that Juan had no other employment-related earnings,

choices.label: A
choices.text: The flower shop must withhold FICA taxes from Juan's earnings.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Juan must pay self-employment tax on the earnings of the business.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Juan will be exempt from self-employment taxes for the first three years of operations.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Juan will be exempt from the Medicare tax because the business earnings are below the threshold amount.

questions.explanation:
A sole proprietor is not an employee of the business, so no FICA tax is withheld from the proprietor's earnings. Instead, IRC §1401 imposes self-employment tax (Social Security and Medicare) on net earnings from self-employment of $400 or more (§1402(b)). Juan's $60,000 of business income is therefore subject to self-employment tax, computed on 92.35% of net earnings.

A proprietorship does not withhold FICA from its owner. There is no exemption from self-employment tax for the first three years of a new business. The Medicare portion applies to all net earnings from self-employment with no minimum beyond the $400 filing threshold; the threshold amounts in the law trigger the additional 0.9% Medicare tax, not the basic Medicare tax.
questions.explanationJa:
個人事業主は事業の従業員ではないので、本人の所得からFICA税は源泉徴収されない。代わりにIRC §1401により、自営業による純所得が$400以上（§1402(b)）であれば自営業税（社会保障税・メディケア税）が課される。Juanの事業所得$60,000は自営業税の対象で、純所得の92.35%を基礎に計算する。

個人事業は事業主本人からFICAを源泉徴収しない。開業後3年間の免除制度はない。メディケア部分は自営業の純所得全額にかかり、$400の基準以外に最低額はない。法律上の基準額は0.9%の追加メディケア税の適用基準であり、通常のメディケア税の免除基準ではない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2017 Recently Released Q.34 (AICPA No. null)

questions.stem: A taxpayer received $200 in interest from U.S. Treasury bonds and $300 in interest from municipal bonds. What amount of interest should be included in the taxpayer's gross income?
questions.explanation:
Interest on U.S. Treasury bonds is included in federal gross income under IRC §61(a)(4) (it is exempt only from state and local income taxes). Interest on municipal (state and local) bonds is excluded from federal gross income under §103(a).

Gross income = $200 Treasury interest

The $300 amount includes the municipal interest instead of the Treasury interest, which reverses the rules. The $500 amount includes both, and the $0 amount excludes both.
questions.explanationJa:
米国財務省債の利息は連邦の総所得に含まれる（IRC §61(a)(4)。州・地方の所得税だけが非課税）。地方債（州・地方政府債）の利息は§103(a)により連邦の総所得から除外される。

総所得 = 財務省債の利息$200

$300は財務省債ではなく地方債の利息を含めており、規定が逆である。$500は両方を含め、$0は両方を除外している。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2018 Recently Released Q.9 (AICPA No. 62577)

questions.stem:
A married couple reported the following items for the current year:

Salaries | $95,000
Dividends | 1,000
Interest income on savings account | 500
Loss from rental real estate | (2,000)

Both spouses actively participate in the rental real estate activities. What is the taxpayers' adjusted gross income on a joint return for the year?
questions.explanation:
Under IRC §469(i), taxpayers who actively participate in rental real estate may deduct up to $25,000 of rental losses against nonpassive income. The allowance is reduced by 50% of modified AGI over $100,000. Modified AGI is computed without the passive loss: $95,000 + $1,000 + $500 = $96,500, which is below $100,000, so the full $2,000 loss is deductible.

Salaries = $95,000
Dividends = $1,000
Interest = $500
Rental real estate loss = ($2,000)
AGI = $94,500

The $95,000 amount reports only salaries, and the $96,500 amount omits the deductible rental loss. The $98,500 amount adds the loss instead of subtracting it.
questions.explanationJa:
IRC §469(i)により、賃貸不動産に積極的に関与する納税者は、賃貸損失のうち最大$25,000を非パッシブ所得と通算できる。この枠は修正AGIが$100,000を超える部分の50%だけ減額される。修正AGIはパッシブ損失を除いて計算し、$95,000 + $1,000 + $500 = $96,500 で$100,000未満なので、$2,000の損失全額を控除できる。

給与 = $95,000
配当 = $1,000
利息 = $500
賃貸不動産の損失 = ($2,000)
AGI = $94,500

$95,000は給与だけ、$96,500は控除できる賃貸損失を差し引いていない額。$98,500は損失を差し引かずに加えている。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2018 Recently Released Q.10 (AICPA No. 63041)

questions.stem: Four years ago, when Cox's spouse died, Cox filed a joint tax return for that year. Cox did not remarry, but continued to provide full support for a minor child who has been living with Cox. What is Cox's most advantageous filing status for the current year?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Single.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Married filing separate.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Surviving spouse.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Head of household.

questions.explanation:
A qualifying surviving spouse (IRC §2(a)) may use joint return rates only for the two tax years following the year of the spouse's death, and only while maintaining a home for a dependent child. Cox's spouse died four years ago, so that period has expired. Cox is unmarried and maintains a household for a minor child who lives with Cox and whom Cox fully supports, so Cox qualifies as head of household under §2(b), which has more favorable rates and a larger standard deduction than single status.

Single status is available but less advantageous than head of household. Married filing separately is not available to an unmarried individual. Surviving spouse status no longer applies because more than two years have passed since the year of death.
questions.explanationJa:
適格生存配偶者（IRC §2(a)）として共同申告の税率を使えるのは、配偶者が死亡した年の翌2年間で、扶養する子と住居を維持している場合に限られる。Coxの配偶者は4年前に死亡しているので、その期間は終わっている。Coxは未婚で、同居する未成年の子を全面的に扶養して世帯を維持しているので、§2(b)の世帯主（head of household）に該当し、独身より有利な税率と大きい標準控除を使える。

独身（single）でも申告できるが、世帯主より不利である。未婚者は夫婦個別申告を選べない。死亡年から2年を超えているので、生存配偶者の資格はもう使えない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2018 Recently Released Q.11 (AICPA No. 60741)

questions.stem: A painter and an accountant agree to trade their services. The painter provides services valued at $550, and the accountant provides services worth $500. What amount should the accountant report as income or expense?

choices.label: A
choices.text: $50 expense.

choices.label: B
choices.text: $50 income.

choices.label: C
choices.text: $500 income.

choices.label: D
choices.text: $550 income.

questions.explanation:
In a barter transaction, each party must include in gross income the fair market value of the property or services received (IRC §61(a); Treas. Reg. §1.61-2(d)(1)). The accountant received painting services worth $550, so the accountant reports $550 of income.

Income = FMV of services received = $550

The $500 income amount is the value of the services the accountant provided, not the value received. Reporting a $50 expense or $50 income nets the two values against each other, but barter income is not netted; the full value received is income.
questions.explanationJa:
物々交換（バーター取引）では、各当事者は受け取った財産・役務の時価を総所得に含める（IRC §61(a)、Treas. Reg. §1.61-2(d)(1)）。会計士は時価 $550 の塗装サービスを受け取ったので、$550 を所得として計上する。

$500 の所得は会計士が提供した役務の価値であり、受け取った価値ではない。$50 の費用や $50 の所得は両者の差額で相殺しているが、バーター取引では相殺せず受け取った価値の全額が所得となる。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2018 Recently Released Q.25 (AICPA No. 65493)

questions.explanation:
A loss on the sale of a personal residence is a nondeductible personal loss (IRC §165(c)) and does not enter the capital gain and loss netting. The municipal bonds, the securities and the investment painting are capital assets, so their gains and losses are netted.

Short-term: municipal bond loss (held seven months) = ($9,000)
Long-term: securities gain $5,000 - painting loss $4,000 = $1,000
Net capital loss = ($9,000) + $1,000 = ($8,000)
Deduction against ordinary income (IRC §1211(b)) = ($3,000)
Carryforward (IRC §1212(b)) = $8,000 - $3,000 = $5,000

The $8,000 amount is the net capital loss before the $3,000 annual deduction. The $16,000 amount incorrectly includes the $11,000 residence loss and then subtracts the $3,000 deduction. The $19,000 amount includes the residence loss and ignores the $3,000 deduction.
questions.explanationJa:
自宅（主たる住居）の売却損は個人的な損失で控除できず（IRC §165(c)）、キャピタルゲイン・ロスの通算にも含めない。地方債・有価証券・投資目的の絵画は資本資産なので通算する。

短期: 地方債の損失（保有7か月） = ($9,000)
長期: 有価証券の利益 $5,000 − 絵画の損失 $4,000 = $1,000
純キャピタルロス = ($8,000)
通常所得からの控除（IRC §1211(b)） = ($3,000)
繰越額（IRC §1212(b)） = $8,000 − $3,000 = $5,000

$8,000 は年 $3,000 の控除を差し引く前の純損失。$16,000 は自宅の損失 $11,000 を含めたうえで $3,000 を控除した額、$19,000 は自宅の損失を含め $3,000 の控除も無視した額で、いずれも誤り。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2018 Recently Released Q.27 (AICPA No. 60745)

questions.stem: An individual acquired 500 shares of stock on December 20, year 1, for a personal portfolio. On March 15, year 2, the individual executed a short sale of 500 shares of the stock. On December 21, year 2, the individual delivered the 500 shares to cover the short sale. Which of the following statements best characterizes the gain or loss on the short sale?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The transaction will be treated as ordinary income because of the March short sale.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The transaction will be treated as a long-term capital asset sale.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The transaction will be treated as a 40% short-term/60% long-term capital asset sale.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The transaction will be treated as a short-term capital asset sale.

questions.explanation:
When a taxpayer makes a short sale of stock while holding substantially identical stock that has been held for not more than one year on the date of the short sale, any gain on closing the short sale is short-term, and the holding period of the substantially identical stock begins on the date the short sale is closed (IRC §1233(b)). The shares were acquired December 20, year 1 and the short sale was made March 15, year 2, so they had been held less than one year on the short-sale date. Delivering those shares on December 21, year 2 does not convert the result to long-term.

In addition, if the shares were appreciated, a short sale of the same stock is a constructive sale under IRC §1259 on March 15, year 2, when the holding period was less than one year, which again produces short-term gain.

A short sale of a capital asset does not produce ordinary income. Long-term treatment is incorrect because §1233(b) cuts off the holding period at the short-sale date. The 60% long-term/40% short-term split applies to Section 1256 contracts (such as regulated futures contracts), not to short sales of stock.
questions.explanationJa:
空売りの日に、実質的に同一の株式を保有期間1年以下で保有している場合、空売りの決済による利益は短期となり、その同一株式の保有期間は空売りの決済日から始まる（IRC §1233(b)）。株式の取得は1年目12月20日、空売りは2年目3月15日なので、空売り時点の保有期間は1年未満である。2年目12月21日にその株式を引き渡して決済しても長期にはならない。

さらに株式に含み益がある場合、同じ株式の空売りは IRC §1259 のみなし譲渡（constructive sale）となり、保有期間1年未満の2年目3月15日に譲渡したものとされるため、やはり短期の利益となる。

資本資産の空売りは通常所得にならない。§1233(b) により保有期間が空売り日で区切られるので長期扱いも誤り。長期60%・短期40%の区分は Section 1256 契約（規制先物等）に適用されるもので、株式の空売りには適用されない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2019 Recently Released Q.29 (AICPA No. 70255)

questions.stem: A retiree invested $100,000 in an annuity that pays $12,000 annually for 10 years. What portion of the first payment should be included in the retiree's gross income?
questions.explanation:
Under IRC §72(b), each annuity payment is excluded from gross income in the ratio of the investment in the contract to the expected return under the contract (the exclusion ratio).

Expected return = $12,000 x 10 years = $120,000
Exclusion ratio = $100,000 / $120,000 = 5/6
Excluded portion of each payment = $12,000 x 5/6 = $10,000
Included in gross income = $12,000 - $10,000 = $2,000

The $0 amount treats the whole payment as a recovery of the investment until it is fully recovered, which is not the annuity rule. The $10,000 amount is the excluded portion, not the taxable portion. The $12,000 amount ignores the recovery of the $100,000 investment.
questions.explanationJa:
IRC §72(b) により、年金の各受取額のうち「投資額 ÷ 期待受取総額」（除外割合）に相当する部分は総所得から除外される。

期待受取総額 = $12,000 × 10年 = $120,000
除外割合 = $100,000 ÷ $120,000 = 5/6
除外額 = $12,000 × 5/6 = $10,000
総所得に含める額 = $12,000 − $10,000 = $2,000

$0 は投資額を回収し終えるまで全額を元本の回収とみなすもので、年金の規定ではない。$10,000 は除外される部分であり課税部分ではない。$12,000 は投資額 $100,000 の回収を無視している。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2019 Recently Released Q.32 (AICPA No. 63039)

questions.stem: As of December 31, the Mitchells were legally separated and maintained separate households for the entire year. The Mitchells have no children. What filing status should Mr. Mitchell claim for the year?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Single.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Head of household.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Married filing separate.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Married filing joint.

questions.explanation:
Marital status is determined as of the last day of the tax year. An individual who is legally separated from the spouse under a decree of divorce or of separate maintenance is not considered married (IRC §7703(a)(2)). Mr. Mitchell is therefore unmarried at year-end, and because the Mitchells have no children and no qualifying person is described, he files as single.

Head of household status requires maintaining a household for a qualifying person (IRC §2(b)), and there is none. Married filing separately and married filing jointly are available only to taxpayers who are married at year-end, and a legally separated taxpayer is not treated as married.
questions.explanationJa:
婚姻状況は課税年度の末日で判定する。離婚判決または別居扶養（separate maintenance）の判決により法的に別居している者は、婚姻しているとはみなされない（IRC §7703(a)(2)）。Mitchell 氏は年末時点で未婚扱いとなり、子どもも適格者もいないため Single で申告する。

Head of household は適格者のための世帯を維持していることが要件で（IRC §2(b)）、該当者がいない。Married filing separate と Married filing joint は年末に婚姻している者だけが使え、法的別居の者は婚姻者として扱われない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2019 Recently Released Q.34 (AICPA No. 58111)

questions.stem:
An individual taxpayer's tax return included the following:

Regular tax before tax credits | $5,000
Current-year estimated tax payments | 6,000
Amount paid with current-year extension | 1,000
Federal income tax withheld | 1,000

What amount, if any, is the taxpayer's overpayment?
questions.explanation:
A taxpayer's overpayment is the excess of total payments and credits over the tax liability. Federal income tax withheld is credited against the tax (IRC §31), and estimated tax payments and the amount paid with an extension request are payments of the year's tax. The overpayment may be refunded or credited (IRC §6402).

Total payments = $6,000 + $1,000 + $1,000 = $8,000
Tax liability = $5,000
Overpayment = $8,000 - $5,000 = $3,000

The $0 amount ignores that payments exceed the tax. The $1,000 amount counts only the excess estimated tax payments over the tax liability. The $2,000 amount omits either the withholding or the extension payment.
questions.explanationJa:
過払額は、納付額・税額控除の合計が税額を超える部分である。源泉徴収税額は税額から控除され（IRC §31）、予定納税額と申告期限延長時の納付額もその年の税の納付となる。過払額は還付または充当される（IRC §6402）。

納付額合計 = $6,000 + $1,000 + $1,000 = $8,000
税額 = $5,000
過払額 = $8,000 − $5,000 = $3,000

$0 は納付額が税額を超えていることを無視している。$1,000 は予定納税額と税額の差だけを見ている。$2,000 は源泉徴収額か延長時の納付額のどちらかを漏らしている。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2019 Recently Released Q.35 (AICPA No. 65633)

questions.stem: Decker, a 62-year-old single individual, sold his principal residence for the net amount of $500,000 after all selling expenses. Decker bought the house 15 years ago and occupied it until it was sold. On the date of sale, the house had a cost basis of $200,000. Within six months, Decker purchased a new house for $600,000. What amount of gain should Decker recognize from the sale of the residence?
questions.explanation:
IRC §121 allows a taxpayer to exclude up to $250,000 ($500,000 for certain joint filers) of gain on the sale of a principal residence owned and used as the principal residence for at least two of the five years before the sale. Decker owned and occupied the house for 15 years and is single, so the $250,000 limit applies. Age and the purchase of a replacement residence do not affect the exclusion.

Amount realized (net of selling expenses) = $500,000
Adjusted basis = $200,000
Realized gain = $300,000
Exclusion = $250,000
Recognized gain = $300,000 - $250,000 = $50,000

The $0 amount assumes the purchase of a more expensive replacement home defers the gain, a rollover rule that no longer applies. The $175,000 amount subtracts a $125,000 exclusion for taxpayers age 55 or older, which was repealed. The $300,000 amount ignores the §121 exclusion.
questions.explanationJa:
IRC §121 により、売却前5年間のうち2年以上所有し主たる住居として使用した自宅の売却益は、$250,000（一定の夫婦合算申告は $500,000）まで除外できる。Decker は15年間所有・居住しており独身なので、上限は $250,000。年齢や買換え住宅の購入は除外額に影響しない。

譲渡対価（売却費用控除後）$500,000 − 取得価額 $200,000 = 実現利得 $300,000
除外額 $250,000 → 認識利得 $50,000

$0 は高額な住宅への買換えで利得が繰り延べられるとする旧制度の考え方で、現在は適用されない。$175,000 は廃止された55歳以上の $125,000 除外を差し引いている。$300,000 は §121 の除外を無視している。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2020 Recently Released Part1 Q.14 (AICPA No. 57753)

questions.stem: Decker, an individual, owns 100% of Acre, an S corporation. At the beginning of the year, Decker's basis in Acre was $25,000. Acre had ordinary income during the year in the amount of $10,000 and a long-term capital loss in the amount of $4,000. Decker has no other capital gains or losses during the year. What amount of the long-term capital loss may Decker deduct this year?
questions.explanation:
An S corporation's long-term capital loss is a separately stated item that passes through to the shareholder (IRC §1366(a)). Decker's basis ($25,000 + $10,000 of ordinary income = $35,000) exceeds the $4,000 loss, so basis does not limit it. However, at the individual level, net capital losses are deductible against ordinary income only up to $3,000 per year (IRC §1211(b)); because Decker has no other capital gains, $3,000 is deductible and the remaining $1,000 is carried forward (IRC §1212(b)).

Pass-through long-term capital loss = $4,000
Deductible this year = $3,000
Carryforward = $1,000

The $0 amount wrongly treats the loss as nondeductible. The $1,000 amount is the carryforward, not the deduction. The $4,000 amount ignores the $3,000 annual limit on net capital losses.
questions.explanationJa:
S法人の長期キャピタルロスは区分記載項目として株主に配賦される（IRC §1366(a)）。Decker の basis（$25,000 + 通常所得 $10,000 = $35,000）は損失 $4,000 を上回るので basis による制限はない。しかし個人段階では、純キャピタルロスを通常所得から控除できるのは年 $3,000 までで（IRC §1211(b)）、他にキャピタルゲインがないため $3,000 を控除し、残り $1,000 は繰り越す（IRC §1212(b)）。

$0 は損失を控除できないとしており誤り。$1,000 は繰越額であって当年の控除額ではない。$4,000 は年 $3,000 の上限を無視している。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2020 Recently Released Part1 Q.17 (AICPA No. 57985)

questions.stem:
West is single, has no dependents, and does not itemize. West provides the following information regarding his current-year's return:

Long-term capital gain | $15,000
Percentage depletion in excess of basis | 9,000
Dividends from publicly-held companies | 10,000

What is the amount of West's AMT tax preference items?
questions.explanation:
Tax preference items under IRC §57 are added to taxable income in computing alternative minimum taxable income. Percentage depletion in excess of the adjusted basis of the property is a tax preference item (IRC §57(a)(1)). Long-term capital gains and qualified dividends are not preference items; they are included in both regular taxable income and AMTI and retain their preferential rates under AMT (IRC §55(b)(3)).

Tax preference items = excess percentage depletion = $9,000

The $19,000 amount adds the $10,000 of dividends, and the $24,000 amount adds the $15,000 long-term capital gain; neither is a preference item. The $34,000 amount treats all three items as preferences.
questions.explanationJa:
IRC §57 の tax preference items は、代替ミニマム課税所得（AMTI）の計算で課税所得に加算する項目である。資産の取得価額を超えるパーセンテージ減耗控除は tax preference item に当たる（IRC §57(a)(1)）。長期キャピタルゲインや適格配当は preference item ではなく、通常の課税所得にも AMTI にも含まれ、AMT でも軽減税率が維持される（IRC §55(b)(3)）。

tax preference items = 取得価額を超える減耗控除 $9,000

$19,000 は配当 $10,000 を、$24,000 は長期キャピタルゲイン $15,000 を加えているが、どちらも preference item ではない。$34,000 は3項目すべてを preference としている。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2020 Recently Released Part1 Q.18 (AICPA No. 59045)

questions.stem:
The following year-1 annual report was received by Clark from the qualified-defined contribution plan provided by Clark's employer:

Beginning balance | $12,700
Employer contribution | 600
Plan earnings | 250
Ending balance | $13,550

What income must be included in Clark's gross income for year 1?
questions.explanation:
Employer contributions to a qualified defined contribution plan and the earnings on plan assets are not taxed to the employee when contributed or earned. The plan trust is tax-exempt (IRC §501(a)), and amounts are included in the employee's gross income only when actually distributed (IRC §402(a)). Clark received no distribution in year 1, so gross income from the plan is $0.

The $250 amount incorrectly taxes the plan earnings currently. The $600 amount incorrectly taxes the employer contribution currently. The $850 amount ($600 + $250) incorrectly taxes the entire increase in the account balance before any distribution.
questions.explanationJa:
適格確定拠出年金への雇用主拠出額と運用益は、拠出・発生の時点では従業員に課税されない。年金信託は非課税（IRC §501(a)）で、従業員の総所得に算入されるのは実際に分配を受けた時である（IRC §402(a)）。Clarkは1年目に分配を受けていないので、総所得への算入額は$0。

$250は運用益を、$600は雇用主拠出額を、$850（$600 + $250）は残高増加額の全部を、分配前に課税してしまっている点で誤り。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2020 Recently Released Part2 Q.11 (AICPA No. 62517)

questions.stem:
An individual partner received a Schedule K-1 from a partnership for year 2 reporting the following items:

Ordinary business income | $45,000
Interest income | 8,000
Net Section 1231 loss | 5,000
Cash distribution | 6,000

No additional partnership items exist for year 2. What is the total amount from the partnership that will be included in the partner's adjusted gross income on the partner's Form 1040 for year 2?
questions.explanation:
A partner includes his or her distributive share of each partnership item on the partner's own return (IRC §702(a)). Ordinary business income and interest income are included in AGI. A net Section 1231 loss is treated as an ordinary loss (IRC §1231(a)(2)) and is deductible in arriving at AGI. A cash distribution that does not exceed the partner's basis is a nontaxable return of basis (IRC §731(a)) and is not included.

Ordinary business income: $45,000
Plus interest income: + $8,000
Less net Section 1231 loss: - $5,000
Amount included in AGI: $48,000

The $42,000 amount incorrectly subtracts the $6,000 cash distribution as if it reduced income. The $52,000 amount misclassifies the items, treating the Section 1231 loss as an addition and the cash distribution as a reduction ($45,000 + $8,000 + $5,000 - $6,000). The $54,000 amount incorrectly adds the $6,000 cash distribution to the $48,000 of income items.
questions.explanationJa:
パートナーは、パートナーシップの各項目の分配割合を自分の申告書に計上する（IRC §702(a)）。通常事業所得と受取利息はAGIに含まれる。Section 1231の純損失は通常損失として扱われ（§1231(a)(2)）、AGIの計算上控除される。持分の税務簿価を超えない現金分配は簿価の回収であり課税されない（§731(a)）。

通常事業所得 $45,000 + 受取利息 $8,000 − Section 1231純損失 $5,000 = $48,000

$42,000は現金分配$6,000を所得から差し引いており誤り。$54,000は現金分配$6,000を所得に加えており誤り。$52,000はSection 1231損失を加算し現金分配を減算する（$45,000 + $8,000 + $5,000 − $6,000）という誤った扱いによる金額である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2020 Recently Released Part2 Q.12 (AICPA No. 503817)

questions.stem: In which of the following scenarios would the head of household filing status be available to the taxpayer?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A single taxpayer maintains a separate home for his parent, who qualifies as a dependent.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A taxpayer with no dependents is the surviving spouse of an individual who died in the current year.

choices.label: C
choices.text: An unmarried taxpayer maintains a household with a 28-year-old son, who earned $10,000 during the tax year.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A single taxpayer maintains a household that is the principal home for five months of the year for his disabled child.

questions.explanation:
Head of household status requires an unmarried taxpayer (not a surviving spouse) to pay more than half the cost of maintaining a household that is the principal place of abode of a qualifying person for more than half the year (IRC §2(b)). A special rule allows a dependent parent to qualify even if the parent lives in a separate household that the taxpayer maintains (IRC §2(b)(1)). A single taxpayer who maintains a separate home for a parent who qualifies as a dependent therefore may file as head of household.

A taxpayer with no dependents whose spouse died in the current year is treated as married for that year and may file a joint return; with no qualifying person, head of household is not available. A 28-year-old son is too old to be a qualifying child (IRC §152(c)(3)), and his $10,000 of earnings exceeds the gross income limit for a qualifying relative (IRC §152(d)(1)), so he is not a qualifying person. A disabled child who lives in the household for only five months does not share the taxpayer's principal home for more than half the year.
questions.explanationJa:
世帯主（head of household）の申告資格は、未婚の納税者が、適格者（qualifying person）の主たる住居である家計の維持費用の半分超を負担し、その者が年の半分超同居していることが要件である（IRC §2(b)）。扶養親族である親については特例があり、納税者が維持する別の住居に住んでいても適格者となる（§2(b)(1)）。したがって、扶養親族の親のために別の住居を維持する単身者は世帯主で申告できる。

扶養親族がおらず配偶者が当年に死亡した納税者は、その年は既婚として共同申告ができるが、適格者がいないため世帯主にはなれない。28歳の息子は年齢要件により qualifying child にならず、所得$10,000は qualifying relative の総所得基準を超えるため適格者にならない。障害のある子が同居したのが5か月だけでは、年の半分超の同居要件を満たさない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2020 Recently Released Part2 Q.14 (AICPA No. 98170)

questions.stem: A partner in a real estate partnership had a basis of $5,000 at the beginning of the year and a basis of $10,000 at year end. The partner's at-risk amount at year end was $8,000. The partner's Form K-1 listed $12,000 as the partner's share of the partnership's ordinary loss. What amount can the partner deduct on the partner's tax return?
questions.explanation:
A partner's share of partnership loss must pass two limitations in order: the basis limitation (IRC §704(d)) and then the at-risk limitation (IRC §465).

Share of ordinary loss: $12,000
Basis limitation: the year-end basis of $10,000 limits the loss to $10,000.
At-risk limitation: the at-risk amount of $8,000 further limits the loss to $8,000.
Deductible loss: $8,000 (the remaining $4,000 is carried forward under the basis and at-risk rules).

The $5,000 amount uses the beginning-of-year basis, but the loss limitation is applied using basis at the end of the year after current-year increases. The $10,000 amount stops at the basis limitation and ignores the at-risk limitation. The $12,000 amount ignores both limitations.
questions.explanationJa:
パートナーシップ損失の配分額は、まず持分簿価の制限（IRC §704(d)）、次にat-risk制限（§465）の順に判定する。

通常損失の配分額 $12,000
簿価制限: 年度末の簿価$10,000が上限 → $10,000
at-risk制限: at-risk額$8,000が上限 → $8,000
控除できる損失: $8,000（残る$4,000は翌年以降に繰り越す）

$5,000は期首の簿価を使っているが、損失制限は当期の増加を反映した年度末の簿価で判定する。$10,000は簿価制限だけでat-risk制限を無視している。$12,000は両方の制限を無視している。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2020 Recently Released Part2 Q.34 (AICPA No. 76307)

questions.stem: Which of the following statements about treatment of net passive activity losses of an individual is correct?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Passive activity losses in excess of passive activity income are permanently disallowed.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Net passive activity losses can be offset against portfolio income in the current year.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Net passive activity losses are suspended and carried forward to offset passive income of future years.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A taxpayer can elect either to offset net passive activity losses against active and portfolio income or to carry the losses forward to future years.

questions.explanation:
Under IRC §469(a), a passive activity loss (passive losses in excess of passive income) is not allowed in the current year. The disallowed loss is not lost; it is suspended and carried forward indefinitely to be treated as a passive deduction in the next year (IRC §469(b)), where it may offset passive income. Any remaining suspended loss is allowed in full when the taxpayer disposes of the entire interest in the activity in a fully taxable transaction (IRC §469(g)).

Passive losses are not permanently disallowed; they carry forward. Net passive losses cannot offset portfolio income (interest, dividends, capital gains on investments) or active income. There is no election to offset net passive losses against active and portfolio income.
questions.explanationJa:
IRC §469(a)により、パッシブ活動損失（パッシブ損失がパッシブ所得を超える部分）は当年には控除できない。否認された損失は消滅せず、繰り越されて翌年以降のパッシブ控除として扱われ（§469(b)）、将来のパッシブ所得と相殺できる。その活動の持分全部を課税取引で処分した時点で、残っている繰越損失は全額控除できる（§469(g)）。

パッシブ損失は永久に否認されるのではなく繰り越される。純パッシブ損失はポートフォリオ所得（利子・配当・投資の譲渡益）や能動的所得とは相殺できない。能動的所得・ポートフォリオ所得と相殺するか繰り越すかを選択する制度もない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2021 Recently Released Q.12 (AICPA No. 62995)

questions.stem:
A taxpayer reported the following in a tax year:

Salary | $122,000
Capital gain dividends | 3,700
Partnership short-term capital loss | (6,300)

The taxpayer acquired the partnership interest during the year in exchange for a capital contribution of $2,750, and there were no additional items affecting the taxpayer's basis in the partnership. What is the taxpayer's adjusted gross income for the year?
questions.explanation:
A partner's distributive share of partnership loss is allowed only to the extent of the partner's adjusted basis in the partnership interest at the end of the year (IRC §704(d)). The allowed portion of the short-term capital loss is then netted with the taxpayer's other capital gains.

Basis in the partnership interest: $2,750 (capital contribution; no other basis items).
Allowable share of the partnership short-term capital loss: $2,750 (the remaining $3,550 is suspended).
Net capital gain: $3,700 capital gain dividends - $2,750 = $950.
AGI: $122,000 salary + $950 = $122,950.

The $119,400 amount ($122,000 + $3,700 - $6,300) deducts the full partnership loss without applying the basis limitation. The $122,000 amount omits both the capital gain dividends and the allowable loss. The $122,700 amount ($122,000 + $3,700 - $3,000) applies the $3,000 capital loss limit, which applies only to a net capital loss; here the allowable loss of $2,750 is fully absorbed by the $3,700 capital gain.
questions.explanationJa:
パートナーシップ損失の配分額は、年度末の持分の税務簿価の範囲でしか控除できない（IRC §704(d)）。控除できる短期資本損失を、その他のキャピタルゲインと通算する。

持分の簿価: $2,750（出資額。他の調整なし）
控除できる短期資本損失: $2,750（残り$3,550は繰越）
純キャピタルゲイン: キャピタルゲイン配当$3,700 − $2,750 = $950
AGI: 給与$122,000 + $950 = $122,950

$119,400（$122,000 + $3,700 − $6,300）は簿価制限を適用せず損失全額を控除している。$122,000はキャピタルゲイン配当と控除可能損失の両方を除外している。$122,700（$122,000 + $3,700 − $3,000）は$3,000の資本損失控除上限を当てはめているが、この上限は純資本損失がある場合の規定であり、本問では控除可能な$2,750は$3,700の利得の中で全額通算される。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2021 Recently Released Q.30 (AICPA No. 502563)

questions.stem: Which of the following taxpayers would not qualify for the filing status of head of household?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A single taxpayer whose spouse died in the preceding tax year and who has a dependent child living in the household.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A married taxpayer with a dependent child in the household who has lived apart from the taxpayer's spouse for the entire year due to abandonment.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A single taxpayer who provides over one-half of the support for a dependent parent in a nursing home but does not have a qualifying child in the household.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A single taxpayer who provides one-half of the support for a dependent child who has lived almost the entire year at a U.S. university while pursuing an undergraduate degree.

questions.explanation:
A taxpayer whose spouse died in either of the two preceding tax years and who maintains a household for a dependent child qualifies as a surviving spouse (qualifying surviving spouse) under IRC §2(a). An individual who is a surviving spouse is excluded from head of household status (IRC §2(b)(1)), so the single taxpayer whose spouse died in the preceding year and who has a dependent child in the household would not file as head of household; that taxpayer uses the more favorable qualifying surviving spouse status.

A married taxpayer who maintains a home for a dependent child and whose spouse has not lived in the home during the last six months of the year is treated as unmarried (IRC §7703(b)) and may file as head of household. A dependent parent need not live with the taxpayer; maintaining the parent's home, including a nursing home, qualifies (IRC §2(b)(1)). A dependent child who is away at a university is temporarily absent and is treated as living in the taxpayer's household.
questions.explanationJa:
配偶者が前2年以内に死亡し、扶養する子のために家計を維持する納税者は、IRC §2(a)の qualifying surviving spouse に該当する。surviving spouse に当たる者は世帯主の資格から除外される（§2(b)(1)）ため、前年に配偶者を亡くし扶養する子と同居する単身者は世帯主では申告せず、より有利な qualifying surviving spouse で申告する。

扶養する子のために家計を維持し、年の後半6か月間配偶者が同居していない既婚者は未婚とみなされ（§7703(b)）、世帯主で申告できる。扶養する親は同居不要で、介護施設を含む親の住居を維持すれば足りる（§2(b)(1)）。大学に通うため家を離れている扶養する子は一時的不在として同居扱いになる。

questions.stem: Which of the following can be subject to the net investment income tax?

choices.label: A
choices.text: An individual who is a resident of the U.S.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A domestic C corporation.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A nonresident alien.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A trust whose unexpired interests are devoted to a charitable purpose.

questions.explanation:
The 3.8% net investment income tax applies to individuals, estates, and trusts (IRC §1411(a)). An individual who is a U.S. citizen or resident is subject to the tax on the lesser of net investment income or modified AGI in excess of the threshold amount.

The tax does not apply to corporations, so a domestic C corporation is not subject to it. Nonresident aliens are expressly excluded (IRC §1411(e)(1)). Trusts all of whose unexpired interests are devoted to charitable purposes are excluded by regulation (Treas. Reg. §1.1411-3(b)).
questions.explanationJa:
3.8%の純投資所得税（NIIT）は個人・遺産財団・信託に課される（IRC §1411(a)）。米国市民または居住者である個人は、純投資所得と、修正AGIのうち基準額を超える部分のいずれか少ない額に対して課税される。

法人には適用されないので、国内C法人は対象外。非居住外国人は明文で除外されている（§1411(e)(1)）。未経過の権利がすべて慈善目的に充てられる信託は、規則で除外されている（Treas. Reg. §1.1411-3(b)）。
